result.summary: CEC's telemetry is genuinely unique in the OOB ecosystem — per-cable/per-pin DC-side current at the load connector (esp. 12VHPWR imbalance), kHz-class transient capture with pre-roll, and per-rail data on consumer/workstation PSUs that have no PMBus at all — none of which a BMC, PSU PMBus loop (READ_VOUT/READ_IOUT class polling), Redfish PowerSupplyMetrics, or DCGM can see. But the current Enterprise/MC tier definitions deliver that value through the wrong pipe: enterprise fleet planes are agentless and network-attached (Redfish over HTTPS, SNMPv3, Prometheus scrape), while CEC's primary link is USB-to-host (requires a host agent and dies with the host, contradicting the platform's own host-independent 5VSB story) and the only network option is 1000BASE-T1, an automotive single-pair PHY that no enterprise access switch terminates without a per-node media converter. On PMBus-equipped servers CEC must be positioned as complementary DC-side granularity, coexisting beside the BMC as an independent Redfish endpoint (aggregatable via AggregationSource), never attempting BMC/IPMI emulation. The biggest drafting gaps are that neither tier defines any northbound data model, security-management surface (certs, RBAC, syslog, signed firmware), or time-sync — all table stakes for a device that will sit on a management VLAN — and MC's "redundant uplinks" has no failover semantics. The Redfish/TLS/SNMP stack plus standard Ethernet plus secure element also puts real pressure on the $50/$80 BOM targets, though 100BASE-TX on the ESP32-P4's native EMAC (telemetry volume needs nowhere near a gigabit) is a cost-honest middle path.

expectations.item: Network-attached, agentless management: all telemetry, alerts, inventory, and config reachable over a standard Ethernet management port with zero host software
expectations.why: Enterprise NOC/DCIM tooling (Redfish pollers, SNMP managers, Prometheus exporters) is agentless by default; requiring an agent installed on every production host triggers software-qualification and security review and is a standing objection to USB-tethered devices

expectations.item: Redfish service (DSP0266) over HTTPS: Sensor/PowerSubsystem-style modeling of per-rail channels, TelemetryService metric reports, EventService subscriptions
expectations.why: Redfish is the integration currency of server/DCIM management (DSP2046 defines PowerSupply/PowerSupplyMetrics; DSP2056 extends the model to non-server power gear); existing exporters (sapcc redfish-exporter, idrac_exporter) then feed Prometheus/Grafana for free

expectations.item: SNMPv3 (authPriv) read access + traps for threshold/excursion events
expectations.why: Legacy but still a procurement checkbox in most NOCs; environmental/power monitoring appliances (e.g. NTI ENVIROMUX class) all ship it

expectations.item: Security management surface: unique device identity rooted in the secure element, TLS server-cert enrollment against a customer CA, role-based accounts (Redfish AccountService semantics), signed firmware with anti-rollback, audit/event forwarding via syslog
expectations.why: Any device on a management VLAN goes through enterprise security review; Redfish itself mandates HTTPS + session auth; the tier table's 'secure element' only matters if these workflows exist

expectations.item: NTP time sync with synchronized timestamps on every telemetry sample and event
expectations.why: Fleet-level correlation (which rack, which PSU, which GPU job) is meaningless without a common timebase; every managed device does NTP

expectations.item: Air-gap / no-cloud operation: full function including firmware update with no internet dependency
expectations.why: The tier table targets 'regulated/financial' and 'defense'; spec B.3 already names air-gap as the design priority — customers in these segments verify it explicitly

expectations.item: Per-module fleet inventory: SKU, serial (factory MAC), firmware version, DETECT link class, port binding, exposed via Redfish inventory and machine-readable export
expectations.why: Asset management (ServiceNow/DCIM) ingestion is a routine enterprise onboarding step for any fleet-deployed hardware

expectations.item: Per-pin/per-cable 12VHPWR and per-rail DC-side telemetry that no BMC or PSU PMBus loop can see, with hardware excursion thresholds and retrievable pre-roll capture
expectations.why: Server PSU PMBus/Redfish reports aggregate PSU output at ~Hz polling; DCGM reports GPU-board power; nobody reports per-pin current imbalance at the melt-prone connector or ms-transient waveforms — this is the purchase reason

expectations.item: Telemetry that survives host death: 5VSB-powered sensing plane keeps reporting over the network uplink during host OS hang/BSOD/power-down, fused with NanoKVM visual OOB state
expectations.why: This is a true out-of-band story BMC-less workstations completely lack — but it only exists if the uplink does not route through the dead host (i.e. not USB)

expectations.item: Coverage of consumer/workstation PSUs with no native telemetry (render farms, trading workstations, CAD fleets)
expectations.why: Workstation ATX PSUs expose nothing standard (Corsair iCUE-class USB links are proprietary, single-vendor); CEC is the only per-rail instrument for the BMC-less fleet segment — the sharpest non-duplicative market

expectations.item: Per-rail energy accounting from the INA228 hardware energy/charge accumulators mapped to Redfish energy sensor readings
expectations.why: Rack/fleet power accounting today stops at the PDU outlet or PSU input; per-rail DC energy attribution (GPU vs CPU vs standby) is a differentiator for capacity planning — scope per OQ-13 (partial, never presented as total)

integrations.system: DMTF Redfish clients / DCIM (OpenDCIM, Nlyte, Sunbird), Prometheus redfish-exporters
integrations.protocol: Redfish DSP0266 over HTTPS (JSON/REST), Sensor + TelemetryService + EventService schemas, OEM extension for per-pin/per-cable metrics
integrations.requirement: CEC Enterprise/MC Hub runs a Redfish service on its network management port: Chassis/Sensor resources per rail/cable/pin, MetricReportDefinitions for streaming aggregates, EventService (webhook/SSE) for excursion events, OEM schema namespace for transient-capture retrieval; validated with the DMTF Redfish-Service-Validator

integrations.protocol: Coexistence + optional Redfish AggregationSource; explicitly NOT IPMI emulation or PMBus injection
integrations.requirement: CEC operates as an independent management endpoint on the same management VLAN requiring zero BMC/board modification; document non-interference (no I2C/PMBus bus attachment) and support being registered as an AggregationSource so aggregating managers present CEC data beside BMC data

integrations.system: NMS / NOC platforms (PRTG, SolarWinds, Zabbix, ManageEngine)
integrations.protocol: SNMPv3 (authPriv) GET/WALK + traps, enterprise MIB
integrations.requirement: Publish a CEC MIB covering per-rail V/I/P/energy, module inventory, and alarm state; emit v3 traps for threshold/excursion/module-removed events

integrations.protocol: NTP (SNTP client minimum); optional PTP (IEEE 1588) on MC where the TSN/FPGA data-plane leaning already provides hardware timestamping
integrations.requirement: All samples/events carry synchronized UTC timestamps; PTP is the MC differentiator for sub-ms cross-machine event correlation

integrations.protocol: Syslog RFC 5424 over TLS
integrations.requirement: Forward audit events (auth, config change, firmware update, plan execution per Appendix D) and telemetry alarms to a customer syslog target

integrations.system: GPU fleet tooling (NVIDIA DCGM) and host metrics (Prometheus node stack)
integrations.protocol: Optional host agent: local exporter endpoint + correlation of CEC per-pin data with GPU job/clock state
integrations.requirement: Host agent is an enrichment layer only (never required for base telemetry); provides a /metrics Prometheus endpoint and joins 12VHPWR per-pin excursions with DCGM job/power context

integrations.system: Appendix D support pipeline in regulated fleets
integrations.protocol: Self-hosted/on-prem deployment of the off-machine swarm/judge; Redfish EventService as the machine-side event feed
integrations.requirement: The pipeline's off-machine zone must have an on-prem deployment mode for air-gapped/regulated customers; plan-signing keys custody in the Enterprise secure element (OQ-62) with customer-controlled roots

gaps.gap: Primary Enterprise host link is USB HS with network only 'optional': an enterprise monitoring device whose data path requires a host agent on every production machine, and which goes dark exactly when the host fails, contradicts both the agentless fleet-management norm and CEC's own host-independent 5VSB value proposition

The one network option named is 1000BASE-T1 — an automotive single-pair PHY that no enterprise access switch terminates; deploying it requires a ~$300-class media converter per node (Intrepid/Phytools class), which kills the tier; standard 1000BASE-T/100BASE-TX RJ-45 (or SFP) is what the ecosystem plugs into

No northbound data model is defined anywhere for either tier — no Redfish, no SNMP, no MIB, no REST schema; 'Regulated/financial' customers cannot evaluate a telemetry product that names no management-plane interface

No security-management surface: the tier table names 'secure element'/'crypto' but there are no requirements for TLS cert enrollment, account/RBAC model, audit logging, syslog forwarding, or signed-firmware/anti-rollback workflow — the things a management-VLAN security review actually checks

MC 'redundant uplinks' has no semantics: no statement of what the two links are (dual Ethernet? Ethernet+USB?), independence of failure domains, failover/failback behavior, or how failover itself is alerted
No time-sync requirement (NTP/PTP) — without it, fleet-level and cross-machine event correlation, the whole point of aggregated telemetry, is undefined

RJ-11 'trust channel' has no definition and no counterpart in any management ecosystem (nothing in a datacenter terminates RJ-11); it is named hardware with no specifying body, no threat model, and no integration story — define it against a real use or cut it

No positioning statement vs PMBus/Redfish-equipped server PSUs: on CRPS-class servers the BMC already reports PSU input/output V/I/P/temp, so an unscoped pitch invites the 'we already have this' objection; the tier definition must scope CEC as downstream DC-side per-connector granularity + transient capture + BMC-less workstation coverage
Appendix D support pipeline assumes an off-machine swarm with no stated on-prem/air-gapped deployment mode — unacceptable by default in the regulated/financial/defense segments the tiers target

$50/$80 BOM targets are unreconciled with what this lens demands (Ethernet PHY+magnetics+jack, secure element, TLS/Redfish-capable firmware surface, MC dual uplinks) — D-ENT-2/D-ENT-3 collision, worse under the PolarFire leaning

Module identity is factory-MAC + database with no hardware attestation (1-Wire/EEPROM path explicitly not adopted): adequate for inventory, but MC anti-tamper/anti-counterfeit provenance of the sensing plane itself has no mechanism — surface at D-ENT-5, not assumed

No stated DCIM/asset-management export (inventory as Redfish resources or machine-readable export) even though all the underlying data (DETECT class, MAC serial, firmware version, port binding) exists

req_candidates.statement: REQ: The Hub SHALL provide a dedicated network management port using standard IEEE 802.3 100BASE-TX/1000BASE-T on RJ-45 (or SFP), with 802.3-standard magnetic isolation (>=1500 Vrms) satisfying the OQ-14 enterprise over-voltage carve-out; 1000BASE-T1 SHALL NOT be the sole or default network uplink and may be retained only as an internal/inter-board link.

REQ: All telemetry, alerting, inventory, and configuration SHALL be available agentlessly over the management port with no host-resident software; any host agent is an optional enrichment layer (GPU-job correlation, Prometheus /metrics) and never a dependency for base function.

REQ: The Enterprise Hub SHALL expose a DMTF Redfish service (DSP0266) over HTTPS on the management port, modeling per-rail/per-cable/per-pin channels as Sensor resources with an OEM extension namespace, supporting TelemetryService metric reports and EventService (webhook/SSE) subscriptions, and passing the DMTF Redfish-Service-Validator.
REQ: The Hub SHALL support SNMPv3 (authPriv) read access and trap emission for threshold/excursion, module-presence, and uplink-failover events, against a published CEC enterprise MIB.

REQ: Telemetry acquisition and delivery over the network uplink SHALL continue independent of host OS state (host hang, BSOD, S5), powered from 5VSB per the existing platform architecture; host-down operation is a verified test case, not a side effect.

REQ: The MC Hub SHALL provide two management uplinks in independent failure domains with automatic failover, defined failback, and failover events emitted on both Redfish EventService and SNMP trap paths; USB is relegated to bench/provisioning roles.

REQ: The Hub SHALL implement a security baseline: unique device identity keyed in the secure element, TLS server-certificate enrollment against a customer CA, role-based local accounts (Redfish AccountService semantics), signed firmware with anti-rollback, and audit-event forwarding via syslog (RFC 5424) over TLS.

REQ: The Hub SHALL synchronize time via NTP and stamp every sample and event with UTC time; the MC Hub SHOULD additionally support IEEE 1588 PTP hardware timestamping for sub-millisecond cross-machine event correlation.

REQ: The Hub SHALL coexist with any platform BMC without board or firmware modification (no I2C/PMBus/IPMI attachment to the host management plane) and SHALL be registrable as a Redfish AggregationSource by aggregating managers; CEC documentation SHALL scope its telemetry as downstream DC-side per-connector data complementary to PSU PMBus/PowerSupplyMetrics.

REQ: The Hub SHALL expose per-module inventory (module SKU, serial = factory MAC, firmware version, DETECT link class, physical port binding) as Redfish inventory resources and as a machine-readable export for asset-management ingestion.

REQ: All functions, including firmware update and (if deployed) the Appendix D support pipeline, SHALL operate with no internet/cloud dependency; the support pipeline's off-machine zone SHALL offer an on-prem/self-hosted deployment mode with plan-signing roots under customer control (OQ-62 binding).

REQ: Hardware/firmware excursion thresholds (per-pin overcurrent, per-cable imbalance, rail deviation) SHALL generate events within 1 s on the management plane, with the associated pre-roll capture buffer (§6.10) retrievable through the Redfish OEM interface.

REQ: Per-rail energy readings derived from the INA228 accumulators SHALL be exposed as Redfish energy sensor readings, explicitly labeled as partial (24-pin-scoped) per OQ-13 and never presented as total system energy.

challenges: 1000BASE-T1 as the Enterprise network option is the wrong PHY for this ecosystem: it is automotive single-pair Ethernet, electrically incompatible with the 1000BASE-T/SFP ports every enterprise access switch has, and bridging costs a media converter per node — the uplink should be standard 802.3 copper/SFP, with T1 at most an internal link (this also reframes the Phase-2 research item 2 parts survey).

USB HS as the primary Enterprise host link contradicts the agentless, network-attached norm of fleet management AND CEC's own host-independent 5VSB architecture: the platform's best OOB asset (telemetry that survives host death) is thrown away if the data path routes through the dead host. USB should be demoted to bench/provisioning on Enterprise/MC.

The $50 Enterprise / $80 MC BOM targets (D-ENT-3) are very unlikely to survive this lens's table stakes (Ethernet PHY+magnetics, secure element, TLS/Redfish-capable firmware surface, MC dual uplinks); conversely, a full gigabit port is overkill — aggregate CEC telemetry (CAN 500k + a few RS-485 streams ~1 MB/s each) fits comfortably in 100BASE-TX, which the ESP32-P4's native 10/100 EMAC serves without an external MAC, offering a cost-honest middle path that also weakens the PolarFire-for-Enterprise argument (Appendix B.5 / D-ENT-2).

RJ-11 'trust channel' has no counterpart or meaning in the server-management ecosystem; as named hardware with no specifying body it will read as vestigial in enterprise evaluation — define its threat model and carrier or drop it (Phase-2 research item 3 should be allowed to conclude 'cut').

The tier table's 'Regulated/financial' and 'Defense' roles implicitly promise a management-plane data model (Redfish/SNMP), a security surface, and air-gap operation that no current spec section provides — the §6 register map in the plan should add explicit 'northbound management interface' and 'fleet integration' slots, which it currently lacks (it has 'host uplink(s)' but no data-model slot).

On PMBus/Redfish-equipped servers, naive positioning duplicates what the BMC already reports (PowerSupply/PowerSupplyMetrics via PMBus); the defensible enterprise wedge is (a) BMC-less workstation/edge fleets whose ATX PSUs expose nothing standard, (b) per-pin 12VHPWR/12V-2x6 connector health invisible to BMC and DCGM, and (c) kHz transient capture with pre-roll vs ~Hz PMBus polling — the requirements and marketing must scope to that wedge explicitly.

Appendix D's off-machine swarm zone, as drafted, is cloud-shaped; the segments these tiers target will require an on-prem/self-hosted pipeline deployment and customer-controlled signing roots — this should be an explicit OQ-62/OQ-66-adjacent requirement, not an assumption.

Tier-agnostic modules (LOCKED) are compatible with this lens for inventory (MAC + DETECT class suffice), but MC anti-tamper aspirations have no module-side attestation mechanism; if MC provenance of the sensing plane matters, the not-adopted §2.3 1-Wire ID path or a CAN-level challenge-response needs an explicit D-ENT-5 adopt/decline rather than silence.

challenges: 1000BASE-T1 is the wrong PHY for this buyer: it is automotive single-pair Ethernet, physically incompatible with 1000BASE-T RJ-45 enterprise switch ports (requires a media converter per link; H-MTD-class connectors, no datacenter cabling plant support). If the Enterprise uplink is meant to reach a DCIM/NMS network it must be standard 10/100/1000BASE-T with magnetics (where the deferred OQ-14 over-voltage answer naturally lands). Keep T1 only if a specific automotive/industrial customer asks for it.

The USB-HS-primary host link contradicts the core ops expectation that power monitoring is OUT-OF-BAND: DCIM/NMS platforms poll network endpoints directly and must keep seeing the device when the host OS is down or the box is off. CEC's 5VSB always-on module network and host-independent enumeration are exactly the right bones — but without a network management plane on the Enterprise Hub, telemetry dies with the host agent. The 'optional' 1000BASE-T1 should become a mandatory Ethernet management port on Enterprise; USB stays as the consumer/host-agent path.

The $50 Enterprise BOM target cannot cover what this buyer defines as an enterprise device: Ethernet PHY + magnetics + protected RJ-45, secure element, TLS/SNMPv3-capable stack, more flash for buffered telemetry, plus the existing P4 base. Managed rack-PDU controllers (the closest analog) are $100+ subassemblies. D-ENT-3 re-baseline is justified from this lens alone; ~$80 MC is even tighter once redundant PHYs land.

Appendix B's TSN-switch/PolarFire data-plane leaning solves a problem this buyer did not ask for: DCIM ingestion is 1-minute-class SNMP/REST polling plus event traps — an ordinary gigabit MAC+PHY on an RTOS with NTP is sufficient for Enterprise. PTP (and thus fancier timestamping) is genuinely relevant only to the MC broadcast vertical (SMPTE ST 2110 plants run PTP) — scope it there, not as an Enterprise-wide FPGA justification.

The RJ-11 'trust channel' has no consumer in any enterprise ops ecosystem — no DCIM, NMS, or BMS tool speaks anything over RJ-11, and an undefined extra jack is a security-questionnaire liability ('what is this port?'). Define a concrete function and threat model or drop it; from this lens its value is zero.

The 'Enterprise = regulated/financial datacenter' framing overstates rack-server fit: modern rack servers use CRPS PSUs, 12V busbars/distribution boards, or ATX12VO — not the ATX 24-pin/EPS/PCIe cable harness CEC modules interpose, and their BMCs already export PSU telemetry via PMBus→Redfish PowerSubsystem (the 'my iDRAC already shows PSU watts' objection). The real served market is BMC-less fleets: GPU workstations, render farms, broadcast machines, trading-desk workstations, industrial PCs — still bought and monitored by the same ops teams, so DCIM/NMS integration remains mandatory, but positioning and any future module SKUs (CRPS/12VO) should reflect it.

Tier-agnostic modules are fine for this buyer (asset inventory via CAN-enumerated factory MAC + database is a workable serial-number story), but a regulated/MC fleet asking for authenticated hardware inventory would need the not-adopted §2.3 1-Wire ID/EEPROM path or SE-backed attestation of the module table — keep D-ENT-5 alive as a customer-triggered option rather than declining it permanently.

Appendix D's support pipeline (remote signed-plan execution on customer machines) will collide with enterprise change-management: it is only sellable if every plan execution, consent, and verification event exports to the customer's SIEM/syslog as an audit trail, and if the whole actuation half can be disabled fleet-wide by policy. That audit-export hook belongs in the Enterprise Hub requirements now, not later.

expectations.item: Network-native, out-of-band telemetry endpoint: the monitoring device has its own IP/management plane and keeps reporting when the monitored host is down or off
expectations.why: Every DCIM platform (Sunbird Power IQ, Nlyte, EcoStruxure IT, Device42) polls devices over the network; agent-on-host paths are not how power infrastructure is monitored, and 'works when the host is dead' is the whole point of power monitoring. CEC's 5VSB-powered, host-independent module network already satisfies the electrical half — the network egress is what's missing.

expectations.item: SNMP (v3) agent with a published enterprise MIB, plus SNMP traps/informs
expectations.why: SNMP is still the lingua franca of DCIM ingestion; Sunbird/Nlyte-class platforms onboard new hardware via its MIB, and legacy platforms are SNMP-only. No MIB = no DCIM onboarding = no enterprise deal in this channel.

expectations.item: REST/JSON API over TLS, with a documented mapping to the DMTF Redfish Sensor/PowerSubsystem schema
expectations.why: Modern DCIM and observability stacks (Device42, EcoStruxure IT, Prometheus-style collectors) prefer REST/Redfish; Redfish is how server power telemetry is already consumed, so mapping CEC channels onto its schema minimizes integration friction and answers the 'how does this sit next to my BMC data' question.

expectations.item: PDU-style alarm semantics: per-metric upper/lower warning + critical thresholds, configurable hysteresis, assertion/deassertion events, delivered via trap + syslog + API
expectations.why: This is the exact threshold model Raritan PX / Server Technology PRO2 established and ops teams' runbooks assume (hysteresis specifically, to prevent trap storms). CEC's internal ALERT/FREEZE triggers are capture machinery, not an ops-facing alarm model — both are needed.

expectations.item: Declared measurement accuracy class per channel, with per-unit factory calibration records, traceability, and a drift/recalibration statement
expectations.why: Rack PDUs set the benchmark at ±1% 'billing-grade' certified to IEC 62053-21/MID; procurement will ask CEC 'what class are you?' even though 62053 (AC revenue metering) doesn't literally apply to DC-side sensing. CEC hardware (INA228 24-pin, REF3030/REF3033 paths at ±0.3–0.5%) can beat ±1% — but only a published system-level spec + calibration story converts that into a checkbox.

expectations.item: Cumulative energy (kWh) at machine level, persistent across power cycles, resettable with audit
expectations.why: Energy — not instantaneous watts — is what capacity planning, chargeback, and EU EED-era efficiency reporting consume; DCIM rolls kWh up from device level. CEC today has hardware accumulators only on the 24-pin (explicitly partial, OQ-13), so total DC-side energy per machine must become a firmware requirement.

expectations.item: NTP time sync (PTP option for MC broadcast), UTC-stamped events, syslog export
expectations.why: Multi-device event correlation and SIEM ingestion require synchronized, standard-format timestamps; every managed PDU ships NTP + syslog. CEC's sub-ms electrical timeline is a bonus, but useless to ops if the wall-clock anchor is missing.

expectations.item: Enterprise network security baseline: SNMPv3 authPriv only, TLS 1.2/1.3 with customer-provisioned X.509 certs, 802.1X EAP-TLS supplicant on the uplink, signed firmware/OTA, SBOM + vulnerability-handling (CRA), audit logging
expectations.why: Any device that touches an enterprise network goes through a security questionnaire; monitoring gear with weak management planes is a classic attack vector, and IEC 62443-4-2-style component requirements increasingly appear verbatim in procurement language. The planned secure element + MCUboot + wolfSSL-FIPS leaning aligns — it just isn't written down as requirements yet.

expectations.item: Fleet manageability: DHCP/discovery-based provisioning, bulk configuration, fleet firmware management, and a DCIM onboarding kit (MIB files, Redfish mocks, validated integration guides for Power IQ / EcoStruxure IT / Device42)
expectations.why: Enterprise means tens-to-thousands of units; per-unit GUI configuration kills deployments, and DCIM vendors certify devices from vendor-supplied artifacts. Cheap to build, deal-blocking to lack at scale.

expectations.item: Per-rail / per-connector / per-pin DC-side visibility with transient co-capture and connector-degradation early warning (12VHPWR ΔT + imbalance, dV/dI source-impedance trending)
expectations.why: This is CEC's genuine differentiator: no PDU (AC inlet/outlet granularity) and no BMC (PSU-total PMBus granularity) can see inside the DC harness, catch a 12VHPWR pin hogging current, or pre-roll a droop event. It is the reason to buy CEC — provided it arrives through the table-stakes channels above.

expectations.item: Environmental context: Hub/module board temps and connector ΔT exposed as threshold-able sensor points
expectations.why: PDU buyers expect a sensor story (temp/humidity ports on every managed PDU); CEC shouldn't import external sensor buses wholesale, but its existing NTCs must surface through the management plane as normal DCIM sensor objects rather than staying internal firmware data.

expectations.item: MC redundancy with observable failover semantics: A/B state (power source, CAN bus, uplink) as monitored points plus failover events as alerts
expectations.why: In the DCIM world redundancy that cannot be monitored does not exist — dual-feed PDUs report which feed is live and alarm on transfer. 'Redundant power/CAN/uplinks' in the MC row is meaningless to an ops team until the failover state is a pollable, alertable datum.

integrations.protocol: SNMP v2c/v3 polling (buffered-data support optional), SNMP traps; dynamic plugin onboarding
integrations.requirement: Published enterprise MIB covering per-rail V/I/P, energy (kWh), temps/ΔT, per-pin imbalance ratio, alarm states; SNMPv3 agent on the Enterprise Ethernet port; trap definitions with severity + assertion/deassertion; a Power IQ dynamic-plugin definition supplied by CEC

integrations.protocol: SNMP (custom device definitions), Modbus TCP (facility side)
integrations.requirement: Same MIB + a vendor device-definition file; optional Modbus TCP register map for sites that bridge IT monitoring into BMS

integrations.protocol: SNMP, REST API, Redfish discovery
integrations.requirement: SNMP for polling plus a stable REST inventory endpoint exposing Hub serial, module inventory (CAN-enumerated MACs, tier, firmware), and rack/host association fields so CEC units land in asset databases correctly

integrations.system: DMTF Redfish ecosystem (BMC-adjacent consumers, PRTG-class NMS)
integrations.protocol: Redfish REST (Sensor, PowerSubsystem, LogService schemas) over HTTPS
integrations.requirement: Map CEC channels onto Redfish Sensor/PowerSubsystem resources (per-rail = PowerRails-like sensors, events = LogService) — either a native Redfish service on the Enterprise Hub or a documented schema mapping for the host agent; this also frames the coexistence story with server BMC PMBus data

integrations.system: SIEM / log pipelines (Splunk, Elastic; enterprise change-audit)
integrations.protocol: Syslog (RFC 5424) over TLS
integrations.requirement: All alarms, threshold events, config changes, firmware updates, and Appendix-D support-pipeline actions (plan received/signed/executed/verified, consent) emitted as structured syslog with NTP-synced UTC timestamps

integrations.protocol: NTPv4 (both tiers); IEEE 1588 PTP profile option (MC, broadcast ST 2110 plants)
integrations.requirement: NTP client with sync-status reporting; MC option to slave the Hub timebase to plant PTP so electrical events land on the facility timeline

integrations.protocol: 802.1X EAP-TLS, customer X.509 certificate provisioning (SCEP/EST desirable)
integrations.requirement: Uplink port must authenticate onto locked-down enterprise segments; secure element holds the device identity key — this is a concrete, buyer-visible job for the currently vague 'secure element'

integrations.system: Observability stacks used by workstation/render-farm ops (Prometheus/Grafana)
integrations.protocol: OpenMetrics/Prometheus exposition (via Hub HTTP endpoint or host agent)
integrations.requirement: A /metrics endpoint or supported exporter — render farms and trading-desk fleets are more often monitored by Prometheus than by classic DCIM; low-cost, high-adoption path for the actual served market

gaps.gap: No network management plane is specified at all for Enterprise: no SNMP/REST/Redfish, no MIB, no management-port requirement — the tier's only network mention is an 'optional' uplink. As defined, the Enterprise Hub is a Pro Hub plus a secure element and cannot be onboarded by any DCIM/NMS platform.
The optional uplink is 1000BASE-T1 (automotive single-pair Ethernet) — physically incompatible with enterprise 1000BASE-T switching without per-link media converters; no ops team will deploy it.

No security baseline (SNMPv3-only, TLS/cert provisioning, 802.1X, signed firmware, SBOM/CRA vulnerability handling, audit logging) is written into either tier; MC verticals (defense, broadcast) will additionally probe IEC 62443-4-2 / FIPS-validated-crypto posture. The secure element exists in the row but has no specified job.

No declared system-level accuracy class, per-unit calibration record, traceability, or recalibration-interval statement — buyers benchmarked on ±1% IEC 62053-21 'billing-grade' PDUs have nothing to put in the procurement checkbox even though the silicon can beat it.

No machine-level cumulative energy (kWh) requirement: hardware accumulators exist only on the 24-pin and are explicitly partial (OQ-13 open). Capacity planning, chargeback, and EED-era efficiency reporting consume kWh, not instantaneous watts.

No ops-facing alarm model: per-metric warning/critical thresholds, hysteresis, assertion/deassertion events, and trap/syslog/SMTP delivery are all unspecified; only internal capture triggers (ALERT/FREEZE) exist.
No time-sync or log-export requirement (NTP, UTC event stamps, syslog) — without it CEC events cannot be correlated with anything else in the environment or ingested by a SIEM.

MC redundancy (power/CAN/uplinks) has no observability semantics: no requirement that A/B state is a monitored point or that failover raises an alert — redundancy an ops team cannot see is treated as absent.
No fleet provisioning/management story (DHCP/discovery, bulk config, fleet firmware update, DCIM onboarding artifacts) — acceptable at 10 units, deal-killing at 500.
RJ-11 trust channel is undefined and has no consumer in any enterprise ops/DCIM/BMS ecosystem; as written it is an unexplained port that fails security review, not a feature.

No positioning or requirement addressing the BMC/Redfish overlap and the physical non-fit of ATX-harness modules in CRPS/12VO/busbar rack servers — the enterprise requirements should name the served fleet (BMC-less workstations, render, broadcast, industrial PCs) and the granularity delta vs PMBus so sales conversations don't die on 'my iDRAC does this'.

req_candidates.statement: REQ-ENT: The Enterprise Hub SHALL provide a standard IEEE 802.3 10/100/1000BASE-T management port (RJ-45, integrated magnetics, over-voltage/PoE-tolerant front end per the OQ-14 enterprise resolution) as the primary telemetry/management interface; USB HS remains the host-agent path. 1000BASE-T1 SHALL NOT be the sole network uplink.

REQ-ENT: The Hub SHALL run an SNMPv3 agent (authPriv; v2c disabled by default) exposing a published CEC enterprise MIB: per-rail and per-connector V/I/P, per-pin current and imbalance ratio (12VHPWR), cumulative energy, temperatures/ΔT, module inventory, alarm states; and SHALL emit SNMP traps/informs for all alarm and failover events.

REQ-ENT: The Hub SHALL expose a TLS-protected REST/JSON API and SHALL document a mapping of all telemetry and events onto DMTF Redfish Sensor/PowerSubsystem/LogService schemas (native Redfish service target; host-agent mapping acceptable at first release).

REQ-ENT/MC: Every telemetry channel SHALL support configurable upper/lower warning and critical thresholds with configurable hysteresis; threshold crossings SHALL generate assertion and deassertion events with severity, delivered via SNMP trap, syslog, and the REST API.

REQ-ENT/MC: The Hub SHALL synchronize to NTP, stamp every event in UTC with sync-status, and export all alarms, configuration changes, firmware updates, and support-pipeline (Appendix D) actions as structured syslog (RFC 5424, TLS transport option). MC SHALL additionally offer an IEEE 1588 PTP slave option for broadcast (ST 2110) plants.

REQ-ENT/MC: The platform SHALL report machine-level cumulative energy (kWh) aggregated across all populated modules (resolving OQ-13 to total-system scope on these tiers), persistent across power cycles, resettable only via an audited management action, with the 24-pin INA228 hardware accumulators as the standby/platform anchor.

REQ-ENT/MC: CEC SHALL publish a per-channel-class accuracy specification (target: ≤±1% of reading for current and power over the stated operating range, ≤±0.5% on reference-corrected channels), with per-unit factory calibration stored in module flash and retrievable via the management plane, a stated traceability chain, and a drift/recalibration-interval statement. Marketing SHALL NOT claim IEC 62053 class conformance (AC revenue-metering standard) but SHALL position accuracy against the ±1% billing-grade PDU benchmark.

REQ-ENT: Management-plane security baseline: 802.1X EAP-TLS supplicant on the Ethernet port with device identity keys held in the secure element; customer X.509 certificate provisioning (EST or SCEP); TLS 1.2+ everywhere; MCUboot-signed firmware with anti-rollback; SBOM published per release with a CRA-conformant vulnerability-handling and support-period commitment.

REQ-MC: Security posture SHALL target IEC 62443-4-2 SL2 component requirements as the design checklist (certification decision deferred to a named customer), and all cryptographic operations SHALL use a FIPS 140-3-validated (or validation-pipeline) crypto module — this constrains D-ENT-2's secure-element/PolarFire choice.

REQ-MC: Every redundant element (power feed, CAN bus A/B, uplink) SHALL expose its live/standby/failed state as a pollable datum, and any failover or loss-of-redundancy SHALL raise a critical-severity event within 1 s on all alert channels; a periodic (configurable) redundancy self-test SHALL be supported.

REQ-ENT/MC: The management plane, telemetry acquisition, thresholds, and alert delivery SHALL operate with the host OS down or absent (5VSB-powered, network-egressed), and loss of the host USB link SHALL itself be an alertable event — formalizing the platform's host-independent enumeration as an out-of-band monitoring guarantee.

REQ-ENT/MC: All on-board temperature sensors (Hub NTC, module NTCs, INA die temps) and the 12VHPWR connector ΔT-above-ambient SHALL be exposed as standard threshold-able sensor objects in the MIB/Redfish model, so connector-degradation early warning rides the ops alerting path, not only the CEC app.

REQ-ENT: CEC SHALL ship a DCIM onboarding kit: compiled+source MIB files, Redfish schema mapping, an OpenMetrics/Prometheus endpoint or reference exporter, and integration guides validated against at least Sunbird Power IQ, Schneider EcoStruxure IT, and Device42; DCIM device-library certification submissions are a release criterion.

REQ-ENT: Fleet provisioning SHALL support DHCP with option-based bootstrap, zero-touch bulk configuration (declarative config via the API), and fleet firmware management with staged rollout — no per-unit GUI-only setup for any managed function.
REQ-MC (SHOULD): Offer a Modbus TCP register map option for broadcast/industrial plants that ingest via OT/BMS tooling; BACnet is explicitly out of scope (CEC is not facility equipment).

result.summary: From the datacenter/IT-ops buyer's seat, CEC Enterprise/MC as currently defined is invisible to the ecosystem that would buy it: DCIM platforms (Sunbird Power IQ, Nlyte, EcoStruxure IT, Device42) onboard power hardware via network-polled SNMP MIBs, Redfish/REST, and trap/syslog alerting, and neither tier specifies any of that — the only network mention is an 'optional 1000BASE-T1' uplink that is automotive single-pair Ethernet and physically incompatible with enterprise 1000BASE-T switching. The platform's bones are actually excellent for this buyer (5VSB-powered host-independent operation = true out-of-band monitoring; INA228/REF-corrected accuracy can beat the ±1% IEC 62053-21 'billing-grade' PDU benchmark; per-pin 12VHPWR degradation detection is data no PDU or BMC has), but none of it is packaged as the table-stakes ops surface: declared accuracy class + calibration traceability, machine-level kWh energy, PDU-style warning/critical thresholds with hysteresis and traps, NTP/syslog, SNMPv3/802.1X/signed-firmware security baseline, and observable MC failover semantics. The honest served market is BMC-less fleets (workstations, render farms, broadcast, industrial PCs) rather than CRPS/12VO rack servers whose BMCs already export PMBus PSU telemetry — which sharpens, not weakens, the case for a standard Ethernet management port and DCIM/Prometheus integration on Enterprise. The $50/$80 BOM targets do not survive a managed-network-device feature set and should be re-baselined at D-ENT-3, and the RJ-11 trust channel has no consumer in any ops ecosystem as defined. Appendix D's remote-actuation pipeline is sellable to this buyer only with SIEM-grade audit export and a fleet-wide disable policy."}

challenges: The RJ-11 'trust channel' as a physical trust anchor should be dropped or formally redefined: no compliance framework (CRA, 62443, FIPS, SOC2 questionnaires) recognizes a bespoke powered telco jack as a trust mechanism; trust must be cryptographic (secure element + signed firmware + attested identity). The spec is already drifting this way itself — OQ-60 rehomes the trust/attestation role onto the secure element and repurposes the RJ-11 for Max power/FREEZE. Also a powered RJ-11 is a physical foot-gun (mismate with real telco lines carrying ~48V battery / ~90V ring), which OQ-60(c) itself flags.

Security is NOT an Enterprise-tier differentiator under the EU CRA — it is a platform-wide legal floor. Vulnerability/incident reporting to ENISA becomes mandatory 2026-09-11 (10 weeks from today) for products already on the EU market, and the full essential requirements (secure-by-design, SBOM, signed updates through a declared support period, CE conformity) bind ALL tiers incl. Hub Standard and every module from 2027-12-11. The tier table's implicit 'security features start at tier 3' framing is untenable for EU sale; only the STRENGTH of the mechanisms (SE-rooted identity, attestation, anti-tamper) tiers up.

D-ENT-2 should be decided by compliance strategy, not raw parts preference: the ESP32-P4 already has Secure Boot v2 (ECDSA), flash encryption, a Key Manager with a hardware-unique key, and an ECDSA peripheral with eFuse-held keys — enough for Enterprise when paired with a discrete certified SE/TPM. PolarFire SoC's real security payload (PUF key storage, DPA-resistant boot, CAVP-certified Athena crypto, anti-tamper) is an MC/federal story; buying it for tier 3 breaks the $50 BOM to solve a problem a $2 SE solves. The split option (Enterprise = P4+SE, MC = PolarFire) is the compliance-coherent one.

The 1000BASE-T1 'enterprise uplink' is an automotive PHY no enterprise network speaks natively, and the moment ANY Ethernet uplink joins a corporate network the customer will require an 802.1X EAP-TLS supplicant with a per-device certificate — which the current summary row has nowhere to store or provision. The uplink decision therefore drags in the IDevID/SE requirement; they cannot be specified independently.

The tier-agnostic module principle (LOCKED) collides with MC provenance/anti-counterfeit expectations: DETECT is a capability resistor and identity is a software-readable MAC (spec OQ-44 itself calls this a weak anchor). Without adopting the §2.3 1-Wire ID path or a firmware challenge-response (the C6/S3 module MCUs have eFuse HMAC/ECDSA capability — no new hardware needed), an MC Hub cannot distinguish a genuine module from a clone. Flag at D-ENT-5, do not assume away.

Appendix D's consent and trust model is consumer-shaped ($25 in-app ticket, end-user rendered consent) and will fail enterprise procurement as written: enterprises require policy/admin-based consent, change-management (ITSM) integration, EDR coexistence for the on-machine agent, signed host binaries (Authenticode/WHQL), and an on-prem or air-gapped variant of the cloud swarm/judge — none of which Appendix D or OQ-61..70 currently addresses. Its architecture (agent neutrality, finite signed vocabulary, judge gate) is genuinely strong and should be kept; the deployment/consent wrapper is the gap.

Espressif (Shanghai) silicon at the heart of a tier marketed 'Regulated / financial' will draw supply-chain-origin objections in federal/defense-adjacent procurement (HBOM/country-of-origin questionnaires are now standard, even where no covered-list ban applies). Not a design blocker, but the Enterprise/MC requirements set should record a position (HBOM disclosure + SE-rooted trust reducing reliance on MCU-internal secrets) rather than be surprised in a deal.

FIPS 140-3 should NOT be attempted as an own-module CMVP validation: the queue alone runs 12–18 months and the full cycle 2+ years. If federal/regulated customers demand FIPS, the realistic paths are a pre-validated crypto library (wolfCrypt/mbedTLS FIPS builds — Appendix B.3 already names wolfSSL FIPS) or a FIPS/CC-certified discrete SE/TPM, keeping CEC firmware outside the module boundary. This must be an explicit Phase-2 decision, not a checkbox.

expectations.item: Hardware-rooted secure boot + encrypted flash + anti-rollback on the Hub (and, honestly, on every ESP32 module MCU)
expectations.why: First question on every enterprise device-security questionnaire and a CRA essential requirement by Dec 2027; ESP32-P4/C6/S3 all support Secure Boot v2 + flash encryption in silicon, so this is a firmware/provisioning discipline, not new hardware

expectations.item: Cryptographically signed OTA with rollback protection AND an offline (air-gapped) signed-bundle update path
expectations.why: CRA mandates security updates through a declared support period; regulated/air-gapped sites (the stated Enterprise priority in Appendix B.5) cannot reach a cloud update service, so USB/host-delivered signed bundles are the deployable form

expectations.item: Per-device cryptographic identity (X.509 IDevID per IEEE 802.1AR) with keys generated/held in a secure element, provisioned at manufacture
expectations.why: Factory-MAC+database identity (the locked Standard posture) is explicitly a weak anchor (spec OQ-44); enterprise onboarding, 802.1X, TLS mutual auth, and the Appendix D unit-ID binding all hang off a hard identity — this is exactly what the tier-3 'secure element' row must mean

expectations.item: SBOM per firmware release (CycloneDX/SPDX) + VEX/CSAF advisories + published CVD policy + PSIRT + declared support period
expectations.why: CRA makes SBOM and vulnerability-handling processes mandatory (full effect 2027-12-11) and ENISA exploited-vuln/incident reporting mandatory from 2026-09-11; US enterprise procurement post-EO-14028 asks for the same artifacts

expectations.item: Tamper-evident, signed, append-only audit log on the Hub covering config changes, firmware updates, identity events, and support-pipeline plan executions
expectations.why: SOC2/62443 evidence chains and the Appendix D audit story both require it; MC redundancy is only meaningful if the audit trail survives power/uplink failover

expectations.item: Remote attestation of firmware measurements (measured boot + SE-signed quote), SPDM-compatible framing as the stretch goal
expectations.why: OCP-style data-center procurement is converging on SPDM/Caliptra attestation for every board in the chassis; a telemetry interposer that can PROVE its own firmware state is a credible differentiator for a device physically inline with server power

expectations.item: IEC 62443-4-1-aligned secure development lifecycle, with a documented 62443-4-2 SL-2 self-assessment for MC
expectations.why: Industrial/OT buyers run customer-led 62443-4-2 assessments more often than they demand formal ISASecure certification, but the evidence pack is the same; MC ('mission critical', redundant everything) is the tier that meets these buyers

expectations.item: FIPS-validated cryptography via a validated library or certified SE — not an own CMVP validation
expectations.why: Federal/financial deals ask 'is the crypto FIPS validated'; CMVP queue is 12–18 months and full cycle 2+ years, so inheriting validation (wolfCrypt FIPS build, certified SE/TPM) is the only schedule-compatible answer

expectations.item: HSM-custodied signing keys and a documented key-ceremony/provisioning story for firmware signing and Appendix D plan signing (OQ-62)
expectations.why: Signed OTA and judge-signed plans are only as strong as key custody; enterprise security review will ask where the private keys live, who can use them, and how revocation works

expectations.item: Vendor-side service posture: SOC2 Type II (or ISO 27001) for the Concierge/support-pipeline cloud, plus DPA-able data handling for diagnostic bundles
expectations.why: Appendix D ingests diagnostics from customer machines; no regulated enterprise will enable that against an unaudited service — the device tier definitions implicitly depend on this service-side posture

expectations.item: Anti-tamper on MC: enclosure intrusion detection, SE tamper response, key zeroization policy
expectations.why: The §1 MC row says 'trust' and Appendix B leans on PolarFire anti-tamper; buyers of tier-4 redundancy expect the physical-security half to be specified, not implied

integrations.protocol: X.509 IDevID (IEEE 802.1AR), TLS mutual auth
integrations.requirement: Factory-provisioned per-device keypair + certificate in the secure element; CA chain published; LDevID enrollment (EST/SCEP) supported so customers can re-key onto their own PKI

integrations.system: Network access control (if any Ethernet uplink is populated)
integrations.protocol: 802.1X EAP-TLS
integrations.requirement: Supplicant in Hub firmware using the SE-held IDevID; without this a 1000BASE-T1/Ethernet uplink is unusable on a controlled enterprise network

integrations.protocol: Syslog/CEF or structured events forwarded via the host agent/Concierge
integrations.requirement: Exportable, signed audit events with stable schema and device identity binding; documented event dictionary so SOC teams can write detections

integrations.protocol: CycloneDX or SPDX SBOM; CSAF/VEX advisories
integrations.requirement: Machine-readable SBOM per firmware release and a VEX feed so customers' scanners can triage CEC components; contractual support-period statement

integrations.protocol: CRA Art. 14 reporting workflow (24h early warning / 72h notification / 14-day final)
integrations.requirement: Vendor-side PSIRT process wired to the platform before 2026-09-11 for anything sold in the EU; product-side telemetry/PSIRT intake to detect exploitation

integrations.protocol: MCUboot/ESP-IDF Secure Boot v2 image signing; detached signed bundles for offline delivery
integrations.requirement: One signing chain covering Hub + all module MCUs; anti-rollback counters; air-gap path where the host agent (or USB) carries the signed bundle with no cloud round-trip

integrations.protocol: SPDM 1.x measurement retrieval; DICE/Caliptra-style measured boot evidence
integrations.requirement: Measured-boot register + SE-signed measurement quote exposed over the USB host link; optional/differentiator — scope to MC

integrations.protocol: API/webhook integration for Appendix D plan approval
integrations.requirement: Support-pipeline consent gate must accept an ORGANIZATIONAL approver (policy-based, ticket-linked) in place of end-user rendered consent; plan artifacts (hypothesis, ops, blast radius, signature) exportable as change records

integrations.system: Endpoint security stack coexistence (EDR, allowlisting, USB device control)
integrations.protocol: Authenticode/WHQL-signed host agent binaries; documented USB VID/PID and device-class posture
integrations.requirement: The on-machine Appendix D agent and the Hub's USB presentation must be allowlistable: signed binaries, stable identifiers, no self-updating unsigned code — otherwise enterprise USB policy blocks the product at the door

gaps.gap: No PSIRT, coordinated vulnerability disclosure policy, or CRA reporting readiness exists anywhere in the platform — and the ENISA reporting obligation lands 2026-09-11, before either tier's board even exists. This is a company/process gap the tier requirements inherit.

No secure-boot / signed-firmware / signed-OTA requirement is written for ANY tier (Hub Standard identity row explicitly says 'no eFuse, no secure element'); the §1 Enterprise row names a secure element with zero specifying body for what it does. CRA essential requirements and every enterprise questionnaire fail on this.

Key custody is unresolved end-to-end: OQ-62 (plan-signing keys), firmware-signing key ceremony, per-device key provisioning at the CM, and revocation are all open. Signed plans and signed OTA are architecture theater until custody is specified (HSM, roles, ceremony, revocation distribution incl. offline).

The RJ-11 trust channel has no threat model, no protocol, no defined payload (Phase-2 research item 3 confirms it's a blank), and OQ-60 has already half-evacuated its trust role to the SE. Carrying an undefined physical 'trust' feature into customer conversations invites security review failure.
No SBOM, support-period declaration, or vulnerability-handling requirement in either tier definition — mandatory under CRA by Dec 2027 and a standing procurement objection today.

No audit-logging requirement: what events, signed how, retained where, exported how, and (for MC) how the trail survives power/uplink failover. 'Redundant' rows exist; the evidence-integrity row does not.

Air-gapped deployment is named as the Enterprise priority (Appendix B.5) but nothing specifies offline signed updates, offline attestation verification, offline plan-signing/revocation distribution, or an on-prem variant of the Appendix D swarm/judge — the pipeline as drafted is cloud-shaped.

Appendix D on-machine agent gaps for enterprise: consumer consent model (no policy/admin consent or ITSM change-control integration), no code-signing/EDR-coexistence requirement for the agent, no anti-replay/expiry/machine-binding stated for plan signatures, and plan verification keys live on the host OS with no tie to the Hub's secure element despite OQ-62 pointing at it.

Module identity remains MAC + DETECT resistor even under Enterprise/MC Hubs; the 1-Wire ID path is explicitly not adopted and no challenge-response alternative is specified — MC anti-counterfeit/provenance ('trust') has no mechanism reaching the modules.

No compliance-regime scoping: FIPS 140-3 strategy (validated library vs certified SE vs none), IEC 62443-4-1 SDL adoption, and target 62443-4-2 SL for MC are all undecided (Phase-2 item 7 exists but the tier rows imply nothing). Cost/schedule of these dwarf the BOM deltas being debated in D-ENT-2/3.

No attestation requirement: 'secure element' without measured boot + a quote mechanism buys storage, not provable device state. For MC in server fleets this is trending toward table stakes (OCP/SPDM direction).

Unauthenticated classical CAN module link (LOCKED) is acceptable for an in-chassis bus but only if the requirements explicitly document it as a physically-protected zone with compensating controls (Hub-side input validation, DETECT plausibility checks) in the 62443 zone model — currently undocumented.
Powered RJ-11 mismate hazard (telco battery/ring voltages into a 'trust' jack) — already acknowledged in OQ-60(c) but unresolved; becomes moot if the trust channel is redefined.

req_candidates.statement: REQ-ENT/MC-SEC-001: The Hub SHALL implement hardware-rooted verified boot (ESP32 Secure Boot v2 ECDSA or PolarFire DPA-resistant boot), per-device flash encryption, and monotonic anti-rollback; all firmware images SHALL be signed, and unsigned or downgraded images SHALL not execute. Verification: test (attempt unsigned/downgraded boot).

REQ-ENT/MC-SEC-002: Firmware updates SHALL be delivered as signed bundles verifiable entirely on-device, over both the online path and an offline path (host-agent or USB delivered) requiring no external connectivity, with rollback protection. Verification: demonstration in an air-gapped test cell.

REQ-ENT-SEC-003: The Hub SHALL carry a factory-provisioned per-device X.509 IDevID (IEEE 802.1AR) whose private key is generated in and never leaves the secure element; the SE SHALL provide signing for TLS mutual authentication, attestation quotes, and audit-log integrity. Verification: inspection of provisioning flow + test.

REQ-MC-SEC-004: The Hub SHALL implement measured boot with firmware measurements recorded at each boot stage and SHALL produce an SE-signed attestation quote of those measurements on host request; the quote format SHOULD be SPDM-compatible. Verification: test against a reference verifier.

REQ-ENT/MC-SEC-005: Every firmware release SHALL ship with a machine-readable SBOM (CycloneDX or SPDX); CEC SHALL operate a PSIRT with a published CVD policy, issue CSAF/VEX advisories, declare a support period of not less than 5 years, and meet EU CRA Art. 14 reporting timelines (24h/72h/14d) via the ENISA platform. Verification: inspection (process audit).

REQ-ENT/MC-SEC-006: The Hub SHALL maintain a tamper-evident, append-only, cryptographically chained audit log of firmware updates, configuration changes, identity operations, and executed support-pipeline plans, exportable to host/SIEM in a documented schema; on MC the log SHALL survive power-source and uplink failover without loss. Verification: test.

REQ-ENT/MC-SEC-007: All CEC signing keys (firmware, plan-signing per OQ-62, advisory signing) SHALL be generated and held in an HSM under a documented key ceremony with role separation, and a revocation mechanism SHALL exist that is distributable to offline/air-gapped deployments. Verification: inspection.

REQ-ENT-SEC-008 (Appendix D binding): The on-machine agent SHALL execute only plans bearing a valid judge signature verified against a pinned key, with plan expiry, nonce/anti-replay, and target-machine binding; the agent binaries SHALL be Authenticode/WHQL signed; enterprise deployments SHALL support organizational (policy/ITSM) consent in place of end-user consent. Verification: test + inspection.

REQ-ENT-SEC-009: If an Ethernet uplink (1000BASE-T1 or otherwise) is populated, the Hub SHALL support 802.1X EAP-TLS using the IDevID, and the uplink SHALL carry only TLS 1.3-protected sessions. Verification: test on an 802.1X-enforcing switch.

REQ-ENT/MC-SEC-010: Cryptographic operations subject to customer FIPS requirements SHALL use a FIPS 140-3-validated module boundary (validated library build or certified SE/TPM); CEC SHALL NOT claim FIPS compliance on unvalidated crypto. The validated-vs-not decision per algorithm is a Phase-2 owner gate. Verification: inspection (certificate mapping).

REQ-MC-SEC-011: The MC Hub SHALL target IEC 62443-4-2 SL-2 with a documented zone model that classifies the in-chassis CAN module bus as a physically protected zone with named compensating controls, and MC development SHALL follow an IEC 62443-4-1-aligned SDL. Verification: analysis (gap assessment evidence pack).

REQ-MC-SEC-012: The MC Hub SHALL provide anti-tamper measures (enclosure intrusion detection logged to the audit trail, SE tamper response, documented key-zeroization policy) proportionate to a documented threat model. Verification: test + inspection.

REQ-MC-SEC-013 (module conformance, D-ENT-5 gate): MC deployments SHOULD support cryptographic module authenticity verification via firmware challenge-response using the module MCU's eFuse-held key (no board change), with the 1-Wire ID/EEPROM path held as the hardware fallback; modules failing verification are flagged, never disabled (preserves tier-agnostic graceful degrade). Verification: test.

REQ-ENT-SEC-014: The 'trust channel' SHALL be defined as the cryptographic trust architecture rooted in the secure element (identity, attestation, signed plans/updates); any physical companion connector (RJ-11) SHALL carry no trust function and SHALL be specified only per OQ-60 (power/FREEZE) with mismate protection. Verification: inspection (spec conformance).

result.summary: Through the security-compliance lens, the Enterprise and MC tier definitions are one-line placeholders sitting under a legal regime that has already started: EU CRA vulnerability/incident reporting becomes mandatory 2026-09-11 and the full essential requirements (secure-by-design, SBOM, signed updates through a declared support period, CE conformity) bind every tier — including Standard — by 2027-12-11, so most 'security' items the tier table implies are Enterprise differentiators are actually platform-wide table stakes, with only mechanism strength (SE-rooted IDevID, measured-boot attestation, anti-tamper, 62443 SL-2) tiering up. The biggest blockers are process, not silicon: no PSIRT/CVD, no secure-boot/signed-OTA requirement anywhere, and no key-custody story for either firmware signing or the Appendix D plan-signing keys (OQ-62). The RJ-11 trust channel is indefensible as a trust mechanism — no framework recognizes it, OQ-60 has already migrated its role to the secure element, and it should be formally redefined as cryptographic trust with the connector kept only for power/FREEZE. Appendix D's architecture (agent neutrality, finite signed vocabulary, judge gate, consent, audit labels) is genuinely strong and audit-friendly, but its consumer consent model, missing anti-replay/expiry/machine-binding specifics, unsigned-agent posture, and cloud-shaped pipeline all fail enterprise deployment, especially the air-gapped case Appendix B names as the Enterprise priority. On D-ENT-2, the ESP32-P4's real security silicon (Secure Boot v2, flash encryption, Key Manager/HUK, ECDSA peripheral) plus a certified discrete SE covers Enterprise; PolarFire's PUF/DPA/CAVP payload is an MC/federal play — and FIPS 140-3 must be inherited via a validated library or certified SE, never an own 2-year CMVP run.

At 100-10k units, the Enterprise/MC tier definitions specify hardware nouns (secure element, optional 1000BASE-T1, RJ-11 trust channel, redundancy) but zero fleet-operations surface: no device-identity/enrollment spec, no zero-touch provisioning flow, no fleet OTA infrastructure, no monitoring-stack integration, and no machine-readable asset-inventory API — and these, not the silicon, are what enterprise procurement actually evaluates (NIST IR 8259A baseline: identity, configuration, update, state awareness). The secure element gives Enterprise a natural 802.1AR IDevID anchor, but nothing says it will be factory-provisioned or enrollable against a customer PKI (EST/BRSKI), and the LOCKED tier-agnostic module principle leaves every field-swappable module on a spoofable software-readable MAC — workable for inventory, inadequate for MC provenance/anti-counterfeit unless the deferred 1-Wire ID path (D-ENT-5) is adopted or explicitly declined. The primary USB host link is an in-band path that collides with enterprise endpoint USB device-control policy and dies with the host, while the alternative uplink is 1000BASE-T1 — an automotive single-pair PHY no enterprise access switch terminates — so the one differentiator MC actually sells (out-of-band, dead-machine telemetry into the customer's Prometheus/DCIM stack) currently has no deployable transport. The EU CRA additionally makes signed updates, SBOM, and CVD legally mandatory (reporting from Sept 2026, full compliance Dec 2027), converting the OTA/security-lifecycle gap from a feature request into a market-access blocker. The genuine differentiators (EOL birth-certificate RMA baselines, 2s pre-roll flight recorder feeding tickets, dead-machine serviceability) are strong — but they sit behind table-stakes plumbing the tiers haven't defined.

expectations.item: Per-device cryptographic identity: factory-provisioned 802.1AR IDevID in the secure element, chained to a manufacturer CA, with customer-PKI LDevID enrollment (EST RFC 7030; BRSKI RFC 8995 for true zero-touch)
expectations.why: The factory-IDevID -> operator-LDevID model is the canonical enterprise onboarding pattern; NIST IR 8259A lists unique logical device identity as capability #1 and regulated/financial buyers (the named Enterprise segment) audit for it

expectations.item: Zero-touch provisioning: unit powers up, authenticates with its device cert, claims into the customer's fleet tenant, and pulls its config — no per-unit console/bench step
expectations.why: At 100+ units per-device manual setup is a deal objection; at 10k it is operationally impossible. ZTP is the standard expectation for any managed device class (network gear, IoT gateways)

expectations.item: Signed fleet OTA with staged rollout, automatic rollback, and update-server integration (hawkBit DDI / Mender-class or vendor server with API), covering Hub firmware AND module firmware distributed by the Hub over CAN
expectations.why: Enterprise fleets stage 5%/25%/50%/100% rollouts with rollback triggers; the EU CRA requires security updates over the support lifetime with vulnerability reporting from Sept 2026 — unsigned or bench-USB-only updates kill both the deal and EU market access

expectations.item: Monitoring-stack integration: Prometheus exporter and/or OTLP (OpenTelemetry) metrics with a documented, versioned metric schema; syslog (RFC 5424) / webhook event forwarding for SIEM and alerting
expectations.why: Datacenter power/health telemetry is consumed through Prometheus/Grafana/Telegraf and DCIM collectors (the Redfish-exporter pattern); telemetry that only lands in a proprietary consumer host app is invisible to enterprise ops and worthless to the buyer

expectations.item: Machine-readable asset inventory / CMDB export: unit ID, BOM revision, Hub firmware, per-port module type + serial (MAC) + firmware + DETECT link class, queryable over the management API — the OQ-44 enumeration report productized
expectations.why: Fleet asset tracking, support entitlement, and RMA logistics all key off CMDB records; the spec already generates this data at CAN enumeration (§2.3) but exposes it nowhere machine-consumable

expectations.item: 802.1X (EAP-TLS with the device cert) on any Ethernet uplink, plus enterprise network conformance (DHCP/static, proxy, VLAN)

expectations.why: Field-swappable modules and hot-spare hubs are the normal fleet maintenance mode; the unit-relative EOL fingerprint (Appendix D.4) makes CEC's RMA diagnosis materially better than competitors — if the swap workflow preserves the history binding

expectations.item: Out-of-band, host-independent telemetry and dead-machine evidence retrieval at fleet scale (uplink powered on 5VSB, persist-on-fault flash egress)
expectations.why: This is the actual reason to buy MC over a software agent: telemetry that survives host death. The platform already has the electrical half (§2.9, D.4); no competitor's in-band agent can claim it

expectations.item: Pre-roll flight-recorder evidence auto-attached to the customer's ITSM ticket (ServiceNow/Jira webhook), not only to CEC's own Appendix D pipeline
