gaps.gap: No fleet management plane exists at all in either tier definition: no provisioning flow, no device-management protocol, no monitoring integration, no config push, no inventory API — the §1 rows and READMEs are purely hardware nouns while every enterprise evaluation criterion at 100-10k units is operational software surface

Device identity is a named part, not a capability: 'secure element' / 'crypto' appear with no requirement for factory IDevID provisioning, a manufacturer CA, customer-PKI enrollment (EST/BRSKI), key rotation, or revocation — without this the SE is a $2 part that does nothing a buyer can audit

No fleet OTA story: MCUboot/signed-boot is an Appendix B.3 exploration lean, not a requirement; there is no update-server integration, no staged rollout/rollback semantics, and no defined path to update MODULE firmware at fleet scale (today modules flash over local USB-C = per-machine bench work; the CAN 500k distribution path is unspecified). The EU CRA makes the update+CVD+SBOM package legally mandatory for EU sale (reporting Sept 2026, full conformity Dec 2027)

Telemetry-egress architecture is in-band and consumer-shaped: primary path is USB into a host app + AllMyStuff/Cloudflare tunnel. Enterprise endpoint policy (Defender/Ivanti-class USB device control) blocks unapproved USB devices and vendor agents on servers; telemetry dies exactly when the machine does; and no Prometheus/OTel/syslog surface exists for the stacks enterprises actually run

The optional uplink is 1000BASE-T1 — automotive single-pair Ethernet. No enterprise access switch terminates T1, so deploying it means a media converter per unit. The one transport that could make the out-of-band story deployable is specified in a medium the customer's infrastructure cannot accept

Module identity remains the spoofable software-readable MAC + DETECT link-class resistor (the spec's own words: 'weak anchor', OQ-44). Adequate for inventory counting; inadequate for MC provenance, anti-counterfeit, and trusted RMA chains in defense/broadcast fleets where a swapped sensing module is a data-integrity event. The §2.3 1-Wire ID/EEPROM upgrade path is explicitly NOT adopted, and the LOCKED tier-agnostic module principle means no Enterprise module SKU can fix it — must be an explicit adopt/decline (D-ENT-5) with the fallback being Hub-attested inventory + module-change-on-port alarming
No zero-touch provisioning / claiming flow: how a unit joins a customer tenant, gets its config, and appears in inventory is undefined; at 1k+ units this is a hard procurement objection

Air-gap/self-host contradiction unresolved: Appendix B.3 names air-gap as the Enterprise design priority, but every defined data path (Concierge host app, cloud tunnel, Appendix D swarm) assumes connectivity; a self-hosted fleet manager with local CA and offline update bundles is promised in spirit (C.1) but specified nowhere at fleet scale

Appendix D support pipeline is consumer-shaped ($25 in-app ticket, end-user consent, CEC-side corpus): enterprise support runs through ITSM, org-level consent/authority, contracted SLAs, and change windows — an enterprise profile of the pipeline (who consents, where evidence lands, when plans may execute) is missing

No audit-logging requirement: regulated/financial (the Enterprise §1 segment) require tamper-evident logs of enrollment, config change, firmware update, and module-identity change; nothing in either tier names logging or its export (NIST IR 8259A capability: cybersecurity state awareness)

RMA/spares workflow undefined: cert revocation on RMA'd hubs, config-class re-binding for replacements, EOL-fingerprint transfer, and spare-pool pre-provisioning are unaddressed — the birth-certificate baseline is a real differentiator that currently has no fleet workflow to live in

RJ-11 trust channel is a named connector with no protocol, threat model, or fleet-deployment story; at 10k units an extra undefined cable per machine is negative value until specified (it may be subsumed by SE + authenticated uplink)

req_candidates.statement: Each Hub SHALL carry a unique, factory-provisioned IEEE 802.1AR IDevID (key generated or injected in the secure element at manufacture, certificate chained to a published CEC manufacturing CA); the private key SHALL be non-exportable. Verification: inspection of provisioning records + test (cert chain validation on sampled units).

The Hub SHALL support operator credential enrollment (LDevID) against a customer PKI via EST (RFC 7030), including re-enrollment/rotation and revocation honoring; BRSKI (RFC 8995) zero-touch bootstrap is OPTIONAL-but-recommended for Enterprise. Verification: test against a reference EST server.

All Hub firmware SHALL be cryptographically signed and verified by an immutable boot chain (MCUboot-class) with anti-rollback and a verified fallback image; a failed update SHALL never leave the unit unbootable or unenrolled. Verification: test (corrupted/downgrade image rejection, power-cut mid-update).

The Hub SHALL implement a fleet OTA client compatible with a standard campaign server (hawkBit DDI or equivalent vendor API) supporting staged rollout groups, health-gated promotion, and remote rollback; the Hub SHALL act as signed-update distribution proxy for attached module firmware over CAN (chunked, resumable, image-verified by the module before activation), with the §3.1 CAN-FD trigger clause re-evaluated if measured module-update time at 500 kbps is operationally unacceptable. Verification: demonstration (fleet campaign across ≥20 units including module updates).

The Hub SHALL expose a machine-readable inventory report (JSON over the management API and at enumeration): unit ID, BOM revision, Hub firmware version, and per-port module {type, serial (MAC), firmware version, DETECT link class, port binding via poke-and-ack}; a change of module serial on a bound port SHALL raise an inventory event. Verification: test.

Telemetry and events SHALL be consumable by standard enterprise monitoring without the CEC consumer app: a Prometheus exposition endpoint and OTLP export (host agent at minimum; served directly from the network uplink where populated), plus RFC 5424 syslog/webhook event forwarding, all against a documented, semver'd metric/event schema. Verification: demonstration (Grafana dashboard from a vanilla Prometheus scrape).

If the Ethernet uplink is populated, it SHALL be deployable on standard enterprise access infrastructure — either 1000BASE-T (RJ-45, magnetics, with the OQ-14 uplink over-voltage protection landing here) or 1000BASE-T1 with a CEC-supplied media-conversion SKU — and SHALL authenticate via 802.1X EAP-TLS using the device credential. Verification: demonstration on a NAC-enabled switch.

All fleet-management functions (enrollment CA, OTA server, inventory, monitoring) SHALL be operable fully self-hosted/on-prem with no CEC cloud or tunnel dependency, including offline update-bundle import for air-gapped sites, at capability parity with the hosted service per the C.1 principle. Verification: demonstration in an isolated network.

Each firmware release SHALL ship with a machine-readable SBOM (CycloneDX or SPDX); CEC SHALL operate a coordinated vulnerability disclosure process, meet CRA reporting timelines (24h early warning / 72h notification for actively exploited vulnerabilities), and declare a security-support lifetime per product. Verification: inspection.

The MC RMA/replacement workflow SHALL include revocation of the RMA'd unit's operational credentials, provisioning of the replacement into the same config class with EOL-fingerprint baseline linkage (the old unit's history marked superseded, never silently inherited), and an auditable swap record; module swaps SHALL be detectable and alarmable per the inventory-event requirement. Verification: demonstration.

(Owner gate D-ENT-5) MC SHALL either (a) adopt the §2.3 1-Wire ID/EEPROM per-module unique-identity path for modules deployed in MC fleets (a spec revision to the not-adopted stance), or (b) formally accept MAC-based module identity with compensating controls (Hub-attested inventory, module-change alarming, controlled procurement channel) and state the anti-counterfeit posture in the security target. No default; explicit owner decision.

Device configuration (alert thresholds, CAN bitrate selection, LED/5VSB power caps, telemetry cadence) SHALL be declaratively definable, centrally pushable to fleet groups, versioned, and drift-reported; configuration changes SHALL be audit-logged. Verification: test.

The host-side agent (where used) SHALL ship as signed, silently-deployable enterprise packages (code-signed MSI, RPM/DEB) configurable via management policy with no per-user interactive consent, with documented proxy support and a published endpoint list — so it survives enterprise software-approval and USB device-control review. Verification: inspection + demonstration (GPO/Intune deployment).

challenges: 1000BASE-T1 as the Enterprise uplink is the wrong medium for the stated customer: T1 is automotive/industrial single-pair Ethernet, and enterprise access switches terminate 1000BASE-T (4-pair RJ-45). As written, the optional uplink requires a media converter per machine, which no fleet will deploy. The fleet lens says: respecify as standard 1000BASE-T (magnetics + OQ-14 protection on this port), or justify T1 with a concrete in-case-harness argument AND ship the conversion SKU. This directly challenges the §1 tier-table row and should be an explicit input to D-ENT-2's parts survey (a T1 PHY + a TSN fabric that never faces a customer switch is stranded cost against the $50 target).

USB as the primary Enterprise host link conflicts with how enterprises manage endpoints: USB device-control policies (Microsoft Defender Device Control, Ivanti class) default-block unrecognized USB devices on servers and managed workstations, vendor agents need software-approval review, and an in-band link loses telemetry exactly when the host fails. For fleet operations the 'optional' network uplink is effectively mandatory on Enterprise and unquestionably on MC — the tier definitions should flip the default (uplink populated, USB the fallback), which also changes the BOM math.

The ~$50 Enterprise BOM target is very unlikely to survive the fleet-provisioning table stakes: secure element + factory PKI provisioning ceremony (a manufacturing-line cost, not just parts), an Ethernet PHY + magnetics + uplink over-voltage protection, and enough flash/compute for TLS + OTA A/B images and audit logging. This sharpens D-ENT-2/D-ENT-3: either the target re-baselines or the fleet feature set decides between P4+SE (cheap, adequate for identity/OTA) and PolarFire (overkill for this lens — nothing in fleet provisioning needs TSN fabric; the security wins are PUF/DPA boot, which a $2 SE approximates for far less).

The LOCKED tier-agnostic module principle + the not-adopted 1-Wire ID path means module identity can never exceed MAC-in-firmware without a spec revision. For fleet ASSET TRACKING this is actually acceptable (MAC is unique and the Hub-attested inventory report covers CMDB needs) — but for MC provenance/anti-counterfeit it is not, and the audit should stop the program from quietly assuming either answer: D-ENT-5 must be decided on the fleet evidence, and if declined, the MC security target must state the residual risk in writing.

Appendix D's support pipeline assumes a consumer relationship ($25 in-app ticket, end-user consent, CEC-operated corpus and judge). An enterprise fleet will not let an off-machine swarm execute signed plans on production machines under end-user consent — authority is organizational (change advisory, maintenance windows, ITSM tickets). The pipeline is salvageable and even differentiating for enterprise (evidence-rich diagnostics into ServiceNow), but it needs an explicitly-scoped enterprise profile; as specified it is a consumer product feature being implicitly marketed to tier-3/4 buyers.

The Concierge/AllMyStuff cloud-tunnel data path contradicts the air-gap posture Appendix B.3 claims as the Enterprise design driver. C.1's self-host-parity principle is the right instinct but is specified at single-account concierge scale; a 10k-unit air-gapped fleet needs an on-prem fleet manager (CA, OTA server, telemetry sink) as a product deliverable, not a principle. Without it, the 'most likely to be air-gapped' tier has no lawful data path at all.

The RJ-11 trust channel should be challenged before any board work: from the fleet lens, everything 'trust' (identity, enrollment, attestation, signed plans) is better carried by the secure element + the authenticated network uplink, which enterprises already know how to cable and audit. A bespoke RJ-11 channel adds a per-machine cable, an undefined protocol, and zero ecosystem integration — it must either acquire a threat-model justification in Phase 2 research item 3 or be deleted from the §1 row.

result.summary: Mission-critical buyers (trading, broadcast, defense, industrial, medical-adjacent) buy monitoring hardware on three axes CEC's tier rows do not yet touch: proof the monitor can never harm the monitored machine (FMEA/fail-passive evidence for an in-power-path interposer), quantified reliability deliverables (Telcordia SR-332/MIL-HDBK-217 MTBF-FIT predictions, derating reports, Class-3/conformal-coat build options), and lifecycle/SLA commitments (7+ year availability, PCN/EOL notice, 24x7/4-hour support, and EU CRA-mandated 5-year security updates that become law for the networked variant in Dec 2027). The MC row's "redundant power/CAN/uplinks" does not match what these buyers mean by redundancy: with modules LOCKED to a single RJ-45/CAN/DETECT chain, the sensing path stays a single point of failure, so the honest and sellable framing is fail-DETECTED redundancy (every redundant element monitored, loss-of-redundancy alarmed) rather than implied end-to-end fault tolerance. Two vertical-fit problems need explicit owner attention: the named MC verticals (defense, broadcast, render, trading) run predominantly dual-CRPS server power architectures with no ATX/EPS harness to interpose, and the two verticals CEC names in its own tier table (trading, broadcast) both live on PTP/UTC-disciplined time (MiFID II RTS 25 100 µs; SMPTE ST 2059), which the tiers nowhere require despite Appendix B's TSN leaning making it cheap to add. Genuine differentiators CEC already holds — per-unit EOL fingerprints, 2 s pre-roll capture, the §2.9 triple-source hub feed — map well onto these buyers if the table-stakes evidence pack exists around them.

expectations.item: Fail-passive guarantee: failure of any CEC element (module electronics, shunt path, Hub, cable, firmware) cannot disrupt the host's power delivery or operation, evidenced by FMEA/FMEDA + fault-injection test on every in-path element
expectations.why: CEC modules sit in series with the machine's DC power (added mated connector pairs + shunts in a 40-55A path); every MC procurement will ask 'can your monitor take down my machine?' before anything else — the IEC 61508-style diagnostics/FMEDA discipline is the expected evidence form

expectations.item: MTBF/FIT reliability prediction per Telcordia SR-332 (MIL-HDBK-217F on demand for defense contracts) plus a component derating report per SKU
expectations.why: FIT budgets and SR-332 predictions are standard bid/datasheet deliverables in telecom, broadcast, and industrial procurement; defense primes contractually require MIL-HDBK-217

expectations.item: Fail-detected (monitored) redundancy: each redundant feed/uplink/bus individually sensed, loss of redundancy alarmed, failover exercised by built-in test
expectations.why: Broadcast ST 2022-7-style practice and datacenter dual-feed norms treat unmonitored redundancy as no redundancy; silent redundancy loss is the classic audit finding

expectations.item: UTC-traceable event timestamps: PTP capability (IEEE 1588; ST 2059-2 profile for broadcast) or host-disciplined clock with documented ≤100 µs bound
expectations.why: MiFID II RTS 25 requires trading-venue members to timestamp within 100 µs of UTC; broadcast ST 2110 facilities are PTP-timed; CEC telemetry that can't be correlated to facility time is unusable in the two verticals CEC's own tier table names

expectations.item: Standard management-plane integration on the uplink: SNMP v3 traps, Redfish/REST telemetry, syslog(TLS) alarm export
expectations.why: Enterprise NOC/DCIM/SIEM tooling ingests these; a USB-only or proprietary-protocol monitor becomes an unmonitored island

expectations.item: IEC/UL 62368-1 safety evidence + UL94 V-0 materials + documented connector current margins for the in-path interposer
expectations.why: Facility and OEM buyers require a safety file for anything carrying tens of amps inside their equipment; CRPS-adjacent power parts are routinely 62368-listed

expectations.item: Lifecycle commitments: ≥7-year product availability, PCN process, ≥12-month EOL notice, firmware/security support window stated in writing
expectations.why: Industrial embedded norms (ST/NXP/TI 7-15 yr programs, VersaLogic 18-month notice) set buyer expectations; MC fleets qualify hardware once and freeze it

expectations.item: Support/SLA menu: 24x7 support, 4-hour-response option, advance-replacement RMA
expectations.why: 24x7x4 and advance-RMA are the standard critical-infrastructure hardware support tiers buyers write into contracts

expectations.item: EU CRA conformity for the networked variant: vulnerability handling, 24 h ENISA reporting, security updates ≥5 years, SBOM
expectations.why: CRA main obligations apply from 11 Dec 2027 (reporting from Sept 2026) to all connected products sold in the EU — a legal gate, not a preference

expectations.item: IEC 62443-4-1 secure development lifecycle, with 62443-4-2 SL2 component certification as target
expectations.why: Industrial asset owners increasingly put 'ISASecure CSA SL2 minimum' in procurement language for anything attached to control networks

expectations.item: Environmental hardening options: IPC-A-610 Class 3 assembly, IPC-CC-830-qualified conformal coating variant, extended-temp build with derating data
expectations.why: Defense/industrial deployments expect a Class 3 / coated option; trading-floor datacenters don't need it — an orderable variant, not the base build

expectations.item: Per-unit birth-certificate provenance: serialized units, EOL fingerprint, drift-vs-own-baseline reporting
expectations.why: CEC already specs this (Appendix C/D); no PDU or BMC competitor offers unit-relative electrical baselining — the strongest differentiator for reliability-obsessed buyers

expectations.item: Anti-tamper + supply-chain evidence for defense: hardware SBOM, counterfeit-parts control (AS5553-style), country-of-origin/TAA statement, PolarFire PUF/anti-tamper leveraged
expectations.why: Defense procurement asks for these before technical evaluation; PolarFire's CAVP/CNSA/anti-tamper story only converts to sales with the paperwork around it

integrations.system: Facility time infrastructure (trading: MiFID II RTS 25 grandmaster; broadcast: SMPTE ST 2059-2 PTP domain)
integrations.protocol: IEEE 1588 PTP (ST 2059-2 profile capable), fallback NTP + host-clock correlation with documented error bound
integrations.requirement: ENT-NET/MC Hub must discipline its event-timestamp clock from the facility PTP domain (natural fit for the Appendix B TSN/FPGA data plane with hardware timestamping) or document a ≤100 µs host-correlation bound; timestamps carried in all exported telemetry/alarms

integrations.system: NMS/DCIM (trading floor and broadcast facility monitoring, datacenter DCIM)
integrations.protocol: SNMP v3 (MIB + traps), Redfish/REST over the network uplink
integrations.requirement: Expose rail telemetry, module inventory/health, redundancy status, and alarms; SNMP trap on threshold/fault/redundancy-loss; Redfish schema for modern DCIM ingestion

integrations.system: SIEM / audit infrastructure (regulated finance, IEC 62443 environments)
integrations.protocol: syslog over TLS (CEF/structured), signed audit records
integrations.requirement: Emit security-relevant events (auth, firmware update, config change, Appendix D plan execution/consent events) as tamper-evident audit records; retention/traceability to satisfy financial-audit and 62443 SR requirements

integrations.system: Industrial control / BMS (SCADA integration for industrial-control buyers)
integrations.protocol: OPC UA (preferred) or Modbus TCP gateway profile
integrations.requirement: Map rail telemetry + alarms to an OPC UA information model or Modbus register map so plant historians/BMS can consume CEC data without custom drivers (can live on the host service layer per the §1 placement principle rather than the Hub)

integrations.protocol: 1000BASE-T (RJ-45) or SFP — NOT single-pair 1000BASE-T1
integrations.requirement: The uplink PHY must terminate on standard facility cabling/switches; if T1 is retained for the PolarFire data plane, CEC must ship the media conversion — buyers will not install automotive single-pair infrastructure

integrations.system: Host out-of-band management ecosystem (servers: BMC/IPMI/Redfish host)
integrations.protocol: Redfish aggregation or IPMI sensor bridge (host-side Concierge service acceptable)
integrations.requirement: MC buyers correlate CEC electrical data with BMC data; provide a documented correlation path (shared timestamps + unit IDs) rather than a second disjoint console

integrations.protocol: Offline signed-bundle export/import (Appendix D adaptation)
integrations.requirement: ENT-AIR needs a sneakernet-compatible variant of the D.2 pipeline: diagnostics bundle exported to removable media, plans signed and imported through the same judge-signature gate, no live swarm connectivity assumed

gaps.gap: No fail-passive/FMEA requirement exists anywhere for an interposer sitting in series with the host's 40-55A DC power path; neither tier row nor §6 defines failure-mode containment or fault-injection verification

MC's entire distinguishing hardware ('redundant power, CAN, uplinks, trust') has no specifying body: no failover semantics, no redundancy-monitoring/alarm requirement, no degrade ladder — and as listed it cannot mean what MC buyers mean, because the LOCKED single-RJ-45/CAN module chain keeps the sensing path a SPOF

EU CRA compliance (vulnerability handling, 24 h reporting, ≥5-yr security updates, SBOM) is unaddressed; legally required for the networked variant in the EU from Dec 2027 — inside this program's ship window

Module MCUs are all radio-capable ESP32 silicon; air-gapped/defense customers commonly prohibit RF-capable parts outright (already flagged as plan §1a.5 but unresolved) — kills defense/ENT-AIR deals if unanswered
No reliability-data deliverables defined: no MTBF/FIT prediction (SR-332/MIL-HDBK-217), no derating report, no ESS/burn-in policy — standard bid requirements in every MC vertical

No time-synchronization requirement despite trading (MiFID II RTS 25, 100 µs) and broadcast (ST 2059 PTP) being the tier table's own named verticals; Appendix B's TSN/PTP leaning is exploration, not a requirement

No management-plane integration defined (SNMP/Redfish/syslog); host link is USB-first, but MC/regulated sites routinely disable USB by endpoint policy — the network/OOB uplink must be a first-class primary path, not 'optional'
1000BASE-T1 is a single-pair automotive/industrial PHY; trading/broadcast/datacenter facilities run standard 1000BASE-T/SFP — as written the optional uplink doesn't plug into any facility switch

Vertical/architecture mismatch: defense, broadcast, render, and trading fleets are predominantly dual-CRPS redundant-PSU servers with card-edge PSUs and power distribution boards — no 24-pin/EPS/PCIe harness exists to interpose; the module family only attaches to ATX-architecture machines, and no requirement or scope statement acknowledges this

MC 'trust' claim vs weak module identity: DETECT resistor + factory MAC gives no per-module cryptographic identity, so a signed telemetry-provenance chain breaks at the module; the §2.3 1-Wire/EEPROM path exists but is explicitly NOT adopted
No environmental/build-grade specification: temp range, IPC assembly class, conformal-coating option, humidity/vibration — undefined for both tiers; defense/industrial buyers ask on the first call
No lifecycle/SLA framework: product-availability years, PCN/EOL notice, firmware support window, 24x7/advance-RMA support tiers — all absent; enterprise contracts require them in writing
No safety-certification requirement (IEC/UL 62368-1, UL94 V-0) for a high-current in-path device — facility and OEM buyers will demand the safety file

Appendix D support pipeline assumes live off-machine swarm connectivity and remote plan execution; incompatible with air-gap postures and with MC change-control (maintenance windows, CAB approval) — no offline/on-prem variant is specified
No IEC 62443-4-1/4-2 posture for the networked variant; increasingly written into industrial procurement as a condition

Maintenance model undocumented: in-path modules can never be hot-swapped (powered-down window required), Hub is swappable without host downtime via §2.9 — true but unstated; buyers need MTTR figures and a spares/bridging-cable strategy in the datasheet

Medical vertical boundary undefined: placing CEC inside IEC 60601-1 medical electrical equipment triggers host-manufacturer component-evidence and ISO 13485 supplier expectations CEC has no posture on — should be explicitly out of scope or a defined 'component evidence pack' offering

req_candidates.statement: No single failure of any CEC element (module electronics, shunt, connector, Hub, cable, firmware) shall disrupt the monitored host's power delivery or operation. Verified by FMEA/FMEDA covering open/short/overtemp of every in-path element plus physical fault-injection test on each module family; the FMEA report is a customer-deliverable.

Each Hub and module SKU shall ship with an MTBF/FIT prediction per Telcordia SR-332 Issue 4 (MIL-HDBK-217F notice 2 available on request) and a component derating analysis at worst-case rated ambient; both delivered as part of the standard evidence pack.

Redundancy shall be fail-detected: every redundant element (power feed, uplink, internal bus path) is individually monitored, loss of redundancy raises an alarm within 5 s on all management channels, and failover is exercisable via built-in self-test without a maintenance window.

The MC Hub shall accept two independent power feeds (formalizing the §2.9 three-source priority-OR; LTC4417-class prioritizer) with automatic break-before-damage failover, per-feed voltage sense, and alarmed feed-loss — telemetry acquisition shall continue uninterrupted through any single feed loss.

Redundant uplinks shall be two physically independent network interfaces with automatic failover; telemetry loss on failover bounded and stated (target ≤1 s of slow telemetry, zero loss of flash-persisted event records).

Hub event timestamps shall be traceable to UTC: the network uplink shall support IEEE 1588 PTP client operation (ST 2059-2 profile capable), with a documented holdover spec; where only USB is connected, host-time correlation error shall be documented and ≤100 µs to satisfy MiFID II RTS 25-class correlation.

The network uplink shall present standard facility Ethernet (1000BASE-T RJ-45 or SFP). If a T1-class PHY is used internally, media conversion is included in-product; single-pair automotive PHY shall not be the customer-facing port.

The networked variant shall expose SNMP v3 (MIB + traps), a Redfish/REST telemetry endpoint, and syslog-over-TLS alarm/audit export; USB shall not be required for any monitoring, alarming, or firmware-update function (USB-disabled sites are a supported deployment).

The networked variant shall conform to the EU Cyber Resilience Act: documented vulnerability-handling and coordinated-disclosure process, ENISA/CSIRT reporting capability, signed security updates for ≥5 years from placing on market, and a machine-readable SBOM (software and firmware).
Development shall follow an IEC 62443-4-1-conformant secure development lifecycle, with IEC 62443-4-2 SL2 component certification as the certification target for the networked variant.

An environmental-hardened build variant shall be orderable: IPC-A-610 Class 3 assembly, IPC-CC-830-qualified conformal coating (connector and shunt-thermal keep-outs defined at layout time so coating is a population option, not a redesign), operating range 0..+70 °C base with derating data and a -40..+85 °C stretch goal.

EMC: emissions per EN 55032 Class A minimum (Class B goal); immunity per IEC 61000-6-2 (industrial environments); ESD/EFT/surge levels on all external ports documented, closing the OQ-14 enterprise uplink over-voltage question in the same requirement.
Safety: IEC/UL 62368-1 evidence for the Hub and every in-path module; all power-path plastics UL94 V-0; every power connector's current rating and measured margin published in the datasheet.

Telemetry provenance shall be end-to-end: adopt a per-module unique cryptographic or 1-Wire/EEPROM identity (the deferred §2.3 path — explicit owner gate, amends a deliberate non-adoption) OR the tier documentation shall state that trust terminates at the Hub and module data is Hub-attested only.

ENT-AIR builds shall carry no RF-capable silicon, or shall document a verifiable radio-disable posture (eFuse/antenna-absent with third-party verification evidence) acceptable under customer RF-prohibition policies — owner gate per plan §1a.5, applies to modules as well as the Hub.
Lifecycle: ≥7-year product availability from launch, PCN process for all form/fit/function changes, ≥12-month EOL notice, and a published firmware-support window ≥ the availability period.

Support offering shall include 24x7 support with a 4-hour-response option and advance-replacement RMA; the datasheet shall state the maintenance model explicitly: in-path modules are replaced only in a powered-down window (target MTTR ≤15 min using CEC bridging-cable spares), the Hub is replaceable without host downtime.

The Appendix D support pipeline shall define an air-gap operating mode: diagnostics bundles exportable to removable media, candidate plans imported as judge-signed offline artifacts through the same signature/consent gates, and all plan execution schedulable within customer change-control windows.

Scope statement (owner decision): either commit a CRPS/PDB-architecture module family (12 V card-edge / distribution-board sensing) to the roadmap for dual-PSU server fleets, or the MC tier's target-machine class is explicitly ATX-architecture workstations/nodes and the datasheet says so.

challenges: 1000BASE-T1 as the Enterprise uplink is the wrong PHY for these buyers: it is a single-pair automotive/industrial PHY, and trading floors, broadcast plants, and datacenters run standard 1000BASE-T/SFP switching — the optional uplink as written cannot plug into any facility network without media converters CEC doesn't ship.

'Redundant CAN' on the MC row cannot deliver buyer-meaning redundancy: modules are LOCKED to one RJ-45/one CAN transceiver/one DETECT line, so the sensing chain stays a single point of failure no matter what the Hub duplicates. Either redefine MC redundancy as fail-detected (monitored, alarmed, honest) or open a spec-revision door for dual-homed modules — which collides with the LOCKED pin table and tier-agnostic module principle.

The $50/$80 BOM rows (now TBD per owner — reinforced here) cannot survive this lens: PolarFire SoC silicon alone exceeds the old $80 target before redundant feeds, dual PHYs, a secure element, 62368/EMC test campaigns, and a CRA/62443 compliance program are priced. MC-vertical buyers pay 10-50x these numbers for evidence-backed hardware; price to the evidence pack, not the BOM.

The named MC verticals (defense, broadcast, render — plus trading from the Enterprise row) predominantly deploy dual-CRPS redundant-PSU servers with card-edge PSUs and power distribution boards: there is no 24-pin/EPS harness to interpose, so the current module family physically cannot attach to most of the target fleet. The tier either targets ATX-architecture workstations explicitly or the roadmap needs a CRPS/PDB module family.

USB as the primary host link fails MC deployment reality: regulated and defense sites routinely disable USB by endpoint-security policy. For ENT/MC the network/OOB uplink must be the primary, self-sufficient telemetry and management path, inverting the current 'USB HS + optional 1000BASE-T1' framing.

Appendix D's support pipeline (live swarm, remote plan execution) is structurally incompatible with air-gapped postures and with MC change-control norms (maintenance windows, change-advisory approval); ENT-AIR needs an offline signed-bundle variant, and even ENT-NET buyers will require execution scheduling inside their windows — 'consented' is necessary but not sufficient.

Module radio silicon (ESP32-S3/C6 across the whole module fleet) vs defense/air-gap RF prohibitions is correctly flagged in the plan (§1a.5) but must be treated as a deal-gate, not a paperwork note: 'unused radio' is not an accepted answer in these procurements.

The MC row's 'trust' is unsubstantiable end-to-end today: DETECT-resistor + factory-MAC identity means module telemetry cannot be cryptographically attributed; the deliberately-deferred §2.3 1-Wire/EEPROM path becomes load-bearing for the MC tier and needs an explicit adopt/decline (D-ENT-5), not silence.

Medical should not be casually listed as an Enterprise vertical: shipping into IEC 60601-1 medical electrical equipment drags CEC into host-manufacturer risk files and ISO 13485 supplier-audit expectations — either scope it out explicitly or define a priced 'component evidence pack' offering.

result.summary: Neither tier definition contains any of the artifacts enterprise procurement actually gates on: there is no lifecycle/EOL policy, no warranty/RMA/spares posture, no MTBF or environmental spec, no compliance file plan (RoHS/REACH/WEEE/CE/FCC), no SBOM/PSIRT/vulnerability-handling commitment (legally required for EU sale under the Cyber Resilience Act — reporting obligations start Sept 2026, full application Dec 2027), and no country-of-origin/TAA posture despite the module fleet being built entirely on Chinese-origin Espressif radio silicon and the Concierge stack including a Sipeed (Chinese) NanoKVM. The good news: the owner's PolarFire direction lands on a US vendor with a formal client-driven-obsolescence longevity program, and Espressif publishes a 12-year commitment on the ESP32-P4/C6/S3 lines, so a credible longevity register is assemblable today. The $50/$80 BOM rows were already dead on arrival (the smallest PolarFire SoC, MPFS025T, is ~$69 at qty 1 from DigiKey) and the owner has re-baselined them to TBD; the market comparison says the ceiling is far higher than the team assumes — enterprises routinely pay $1.5k–$3k list (~$60–120 per monitored point) for outlet-metered rack PDUs, and CEC's per-rail DC-side telemetry has no direct competitor, so the re-baseline should be anchored on value pricing plus the real cost of compliance, certification, documentation, and a 5-year support tail, not bare BOM. The single biggest structural finding: for defense/gov and air-gapped buyers, the LOCKED tier-agnostic-module principle collides with procurement reality (COO, radio silicon, weak per-module identity), which the plan's D-ENT-4/D-ENT-5 gates must resolve with procurement criteria, not just RF criteria.

expectations.item: Published product lifecycle policy: >=5 years availability from GA, spares/RMA support ~5 years past end-of-sale, 6-12 month EOL notice with last-time-buy
expectations.why: Industry norm the buyer can verify: HPE supports networking products 5 years from end-of-sale; Cisco ties warranty to a published Last Date of Support; Dell/Extreme define 5-year post-EOS windows. Enterprise refresh cycles are 5-7 years and a 'mission critical' label implies longer; procurement questionnaires ask for the policy document by name

expectations.item: Component longevity + second-source register for all load-bearing silicon
expectations.why: Vendor risk assessments ask how the supplier manages obsolescence. Achievable now: Microchip runs a formal client-driven-obsolescence longevity practice (PolarFire), Espressif commits 12 years on ESP32-P4 (from Jan 2025); single-source parts (LTC2358-18, TPS2121, secure element) need documented lifetime-buy or alternate-part mitigation

expectations.item: Compliance file per SKU: CE DoC (EMC + RoHS 2011/65/EU), REACH SVHC declaration, WEEE registration, FCC Part 15; certificates deliverable on request
expectations.why: Legally required to sell in the EU and asked for verbatim in enterprise supplier onboarding. CEC currently has zero compliance-plan text for either tier; the plan's Phase-2 item 7 (compliance scan) must produce this as a deliverable list, not just EMC test intent

expectations.item: EU Cyber Resilience Act conformance: SBOM per firmware release (CycloneDX/SPDX), coordinated vulnerability disclosure + PSIRT contact, actively-exploited-vulnerability reporting (obligation live Sept 2026), security updates for a declared support period
expectations.why: CEC hubs are 'products with digital elements'; ENT-NET with a network uplink plausibly lands in an elevated CRA class. IEC 62443-4-1/4-2 alignment is the recognized route and doubles as the answer to enterprise security questionnaires

expectations.item: Warranty >=3 years (5 for Mission Critical) with an advance-replacement RMA option and published FRU/spares SKU list
expectations.why: Dell/HPE/Extreme set the norm (advance NBD replacement at least early-life, 5-year basic hardware service on enterprise networking); a monitoring device that requires opening a production machine to swap makes advance-replacement and cable/module FRU availability more, not less, important

expectations.item: Documentation pack: real datasheet per SKU, MTBF prediction (Telcordia SR-332 class), operating environment spec (temp/humidity/altitude), mechanical drawings, safety/EMC cert copies
expectations.why: Standard attachments to any enterprise RFQ response; MC buyers additionally expect an FMEA or at least a failure-mode narrative for the redundancy claims (redundant power/CAN/uplinks are currently words in a table with no failure semantics)

expectations.item: TAA compliance posture + full country-of-origin register; NDAA Section 889/5949 representation capability
expectations.why: Gates the federal/defense segment only — but that segment is exactly who buys air-gapped (ENT-AIR) monitoring. TAA requires manufacture or substantial transformation in a designated country (China excluded; simple assembly/labeling does not transform), so an Espressif-module-based system needs a real analysis, not a checkbox

expectations.item: Per-unit serialized identity on every orderable unit (hub AND module), scannable, feeding customer CMDB/asset management
expectations.why: Fleet operators track assets, warranty entitlement, and spares by serial. Hub gets this free via the secure element; modules today have only DETECT resistor + factory MAC + vendor database — insufficient for offline/air-gapped asset audit. The spec's unadopted §2.3 1-Wire ID/EEPROM path is the ready-made fix (D-ENT-5 line item)

expectations.item: Anti-counterfeit sourcing discipline: authorized-distributor-only production BOMs, lot/date-code traceability retained per build
expectations.why: AS5553-style flow-down is standard in defense supply chains and increasingly in enterprise vendor questionnaires; cheap for CEC to commit to now (the repo already sources by LCSC/MPN) and expensive to retrofit

expectations.item: Vendor-side security/organizational attestations for the Appendix D support pipeline (SOC 2 Type II or ISO 27001 on the service that receives diagnostics and signs fix plans)
expectations.why: The moment CEC's service can push signed remediation plans to customer machines, it enters the customer's third-party-risk program at the same level as an RMM vendor; procurement will demand audit reports before the tier-3/4 hardware can even be quoted with the service attached

integrations.protocol: FAR 52.204-24/25 representations; TAA substantial-transformation documentation
integrations.requirement: Maintain a per-SKU country-of-origin register (every component's COO + final assembly location), a substantial-transformation analysis for the assembled product, and the ability to certify no covered-entity (Huawei/ZTE/Hikvision/Dahua/Hytera) content; make the Sipeed NanoKVM strictly optional/excludable from any gov-quoted configuration

integrations.protocol: CE Declaration of Conformity; REACH Art. 33 SVHC declaration; WEEE producer registration; CRA technical documentation + ENISA vulnerability reporting
integrations.requirement: Per-SKU compliance file under document control; SBOM generation (CycloneDX or SPDX) wired into the firmware release pipeline; a published vulnerability-disclosure policy and PSIRT contact; declared security-update support period per product

integrations.protocol: Serialized barcode/QR label + machine-readable identity over the host link (USB descriptor / management API exposing serial, model, firmware version, per-module inventory)
integrations.requirement: Hub must enumerate itself and every attached module with per-unit serials and firmware versions so the fleet is auditable without the CEC cloud database — which for modules requires resolving the §2.3 1-Wire/EEPROM identity gate (DETECT+MAC+vendor-DB does not survive an air-gapped asset audit)

integrations.system: Vendor third-party-risk programs (SIG/CAIQ questionnaires, IEC 62443 alignment)
integrations.protocol: SIG Lite/Core, CAIQ, IEC 62443-4-1 SDL evidence
integrations.requirement: A standing answers pack: secure development lifecycle description, key-custody model for the secure element and Appendix D plan-signing keys, data-flow diagram for the support pipeline (what diagnostics leave the machine), and SOC 2/ISO 27001 scope if the hosted service is part of the offer

integrations.protocol: Telcordia SR-332 (or MIL-HDBK-217F) MTBF prediction report; FMEA for MC redundancy
integrations.requirement: Publish predicted MTBF per hub SKU and demonstrate the MC failover semantics (redundant power/CAN/uplink switchover behavior, detection latency, alarm on loss-of-redundancy) — a redundancy feature with no monitored/alarmed degraded state fails datacenter design review

integrations.protocol: Published FRU catalog + advance-replacement RMA process
integrations.requirement: Every field-replaceable element gets an orderable SKU with committed availability: hubs, each module family, the female-female 24-pin bridging cable, 12VHPWR pigtail assemblies, RJ-45 harness lengths; the mezzanine integrated appliance must still decompose into separately orderable hub and 24-pin FRUs

gaps.gap: No product lifecycle policy anywhere in the spec or tier definitions: no availability commitment, no spares window, no EOL/EOS notice process, no last-time-buy. For a tier literally named 'Mission Critical' this is the first question an enterprise buyer asks and there is no answer

No CRA/security-lifecycle posture: no SBOM, no vulnerability-disclosure policy, no PSIRT, no declared firmware-support duration. EU sale of either tier becomes non-compliant as CRA obligations phase in (reporting Sept 2026, full Dec 2027); enterprise security questionnaires fail on the same absences even outside the EU

Tier definitions are bare-BOM rows with no compliance, certification, documentation, warranty, or support-cost dimension — the actual cost structure of enterprise hardware. The $50/$80 targets were set as if the product were the board; owner has moved them to TBD (D-ENT-3) but the re-baseline framing in the plan is still parts-costing-shaped (Phase-2 item 1 sizes the PolarFire part, not the compliance/support tail)

No country-of-origin/TAA posture, and the platform's structural exposure is undocumented: all module MCUs are Espressif (Chinese vendor, China COO), the NanoKVM is Sipeed (Chinese video-capture device), and assembly is quoted against JLCPCB/LCSC. None of this is disqualifying for commercial enterprise, but it forecloses the federal/defense segment that ENT-AIR most plausibly serves, and the plan's §1a.5 flag covers only the RF dimension, not procurement provenance

Module identity is too weak for enterprise fleet procurement: DETECT resistor + factory MAC + vendor database gives no per-unit serial verifiable offline, no anti-counterfeit anchor, no CMDB-grade asset identity. The §2.3 1-Wire ID/EEPROM upgrade path exists in the spec but is explicitly not adopted; it is a D-ENT-5 line item with real procurement weight, not a nice-to-have

No reliability or environmental specification: no MTBF prediction, no operating temp/humidity range, no FMEA for the MC redundancy set. 'Redundant power/CAN/uplinks' has no failure semantics, no degraded-state alarm definition, and no quantified availability claim — unreviewable by a datacenter engineering team

No warranty/RMA/spares definition: no warranty term, no advance-replacement option, no FRU catalog. Interposer products (in the PSU power path of a production machine) make swap logistics a purchase criterion, not an afterthought

Second-source posture undocumented: the design leans on several sole-source precision parts (LTC2358-18, TPS2121/LTC4417, specific INA family parts, the yet-unchosen secure element) with no recorded obsolescence mitigation; the shunt part (OQ-11) is still open with a single candidate

Support pipeline (Appendix D) has no vendor-trust/attestation plan: signed-plan execution on customer machines requires the CEC service side to pass third-party-risk review (SOC 2/ISO 27001, key-custody documentation), which is unmentioned in OQ-61..74

req_candidates.statement: CEC shall publish a product lifecycle policy for Enterprise/MC SKUs committing to: >=5 years orderable availability from GA, >=5 years spares and RMA support after end-of-sale, and >=12 months written EOL notice with a last-time-buy window; the policy document is a controlled deliverable referenced from the datasheet.

Every load-bearing semiconductor on an Enterprise/MC BOM shall be selected from a vendor with a published longevity program (e.g., Microchip client-driven obsolescence for PolarFire; Espressif 12-year commitment for ESP32-P4/C6), recorded in a component-longevity register that lists per-part longevity basis, second source or documented lifetime-buy/redesign mitigation, and review date.

Each Enterprise/MC SKU shall carry a compliance file under document control containing: CE Declaration of Conformity (EMC directive + RoHS 2011/65/EU), REACH Art. 33 SVHC declaration, WEEE producer registration evidence, and FCC Part 15 verification — deliverable to customers on request.

The firmware release pipeline shall emit a machine-readable SBOM (CycloneDX or SPDX) per release; CEC shall publish a coordinated vulnerability disclosure policy with a PSIRT contact and commit to security updates for a declared support period of >=5 years from end-of-sale, satisfying EU CRA vulnerability-handling requirements (Annex I Part II) before first EU shipment.
Enterprise/MC hubs shall ship with a Telcordia SR-332 (or equivalent) MTBF prediction and a specified operating environment (temperature, humidity, altitude) in the datasheet.

The MC redundancy set (power, CAN, uplinks) shall have defined failover semantics: detection latency, switchover behavior, and a monitored + alarmed loss-of-redundancy state, backed by an FMEA covering each redundant element; an unalarmed degraded state is non-conformant.

Warranty shall be >=3 years (Enterprise) / >=5 years (Mission Critical) with an advance-replacement RMA option; a published FRU catalog shall give every field-replaceable element (hub, each module family, bridging/pigtail cable assemblies, RJ-45 harnesses) an orderable SKU with availability tied to the lifecycle policy.

Every orderable unit (hub and module) shall carry a per-unit serialized identity: scannable label plus machine-readable enumeration over the host link (model, serial, firmware version, attached-module inventory), auditable without connectivity to any CEC service; the module-side mechanism (adoption of the §2.3 1-Wire ID/EEPROM path vs label-only) is an explicit owner gate under D-ENT-5.

For the ENT-AIR variant and any government-quoted configuration: CEC shall maintain a per-SKU country-of-origin register and substantial-transformation analysis sufficient to answer TAA and NDAA Section 889/5949 representations; the Sipeed NanoKVM shall be optional and excludable from all such configurations; whether ENT-AIR requires TAA-designated-country assembly and non-Chinese-origin module MCUs is an owner gate rider on D-ENT-5, decided with evidence, not assumed either way.
Production BOM procurement shall be authorized-distributor-only with lot/date-code traceability retained per build (AS5553-aligned counterfeit-avoidance posture).

The D-ENT-3 BOM/price re-baseline shall be computed as a full cost model — BOM plus certification, compliance documentation, warranty reserve, and the 5-year support/spares tail — and anchored against market comparables (outlet-metered intelligent PDUs at roughly $60–120 list per monitored point), not against the retired $50 bare-BOM row.

challenges: $50 Enterprise BOM target vs PolarFire: the smallest PolarFire SoC (MPFS025T) alone lists ~$69 at qty 1 on DigiKey — the row was never achievable with the Appendix B.5 architecture. The owner has already moved BOM to TBD (D-ENT-3); this lens adds that the re-baseline should not even be BOM-shaped: enterprise buyers of comparable monitoring hardware pay $1.5k–3k list per metered PDU (~$60–120/monitored point), so the binding constraint is the compliance/support cost tail and value pricing, not parts cost.

Tier-agnostic modules (LOCKED) collide with regulated-segment procurement, not just RF policy: every module MCU is Espressif — a Chinese vendor with China country-of-origin — which is a TAA substantial-transformation problem and a standing vendor-risk-questionnaire flag for the defense/gov buyers ENT-AIR targets, independent of the plan's §1a.5 radio-silicon question. Espressif is NOT NDAA-889-covered (that list is Huawei/ZTE/Hikvision/Dahua/Hytera), so commercial enterprise is fine; the challenge is scoped to ENT-AIR/gov and should ride D-ENT-5 as a provenance criterion, not only an RF one.

The Sipeed NanoKVM in the Concierge/Appendix C stack is a Chinese-origin video-capture device attached to customer machines. Not 889-covered today, but it is exactly the class of component gov and high-security procurement excludes; every Enterprise/MC configuration must be quotable and fully functional without it.

Optional 1000BASE-T1 uplink is a procurement oddity: T1 is an automotive/industrial single-pair PHY — no datacenter switch has T1 ports, so every deployment needs media converters. If ENT-NET's uplink is meant to be the primary management path (which enterprise buyers expect — PDU/BMC-style out-of-band Ethernet, not USB tethered to the monitored host), standard 1000BASE-T is what the ecosystem integrates with; T1's niche should be justified or dropped in the Phase-2 uplink survey.

USB-as-primary-host-link inherited from lower tiers undercuts the Enterprise serviceability story: a monitoring device whose management path dies with the machine it monitors fails the basic out-of-band expectation; ENT-NET should invert the hierarchy (network management primary, USB secondary/debug).

The Appendix D support pipeline is specified as a technical loop (OQ-61..74) with no vendor-trust half: remote diagnostics plus signed remediation on customer machines puts CEC-the-company into customers' third-party-risk programs, requiring SOC 2/ISO 27001-class attestation, key-custody documentation, and data-flow disclosure — a business capability the requirements program should schedule alongside the hardware, since it gates the same deals.

The mezzanine integrated-appliance form is procurement-friendly (one SKU, one asset) only if the FRU model still decomposes: hub and 24-pin module must remain separately orderable spares or the appliance worsens, not improves, the RMA story.

result.summary: From an OEM/systems-integrator viewpoint the Enterprise/MC tier definitions are hardware-first and integration-blind: neither tier defines a host-side software surface (drivers, API, data formats, monitoring-stack integration), a mechanical/mounting story for the Hub or the per-rail interposers inside 1U/2U chassis and workstations, or a white-label/ODM program — and those, not the MCU choice, are what enterprise deals are won or lost on. The optional 1000BASE-T1 uplink is the wrong physical layer for this market: it is an automotive/industrial single-pair standard with ~15 m reach and zero presence in enterprise switching, so every networked deployment would need media converters; integrators will demand standard 1000BASE-T RJ-45 (with the OQ-14 over-voltage protection that finally attaches there), and PoE powering is worth evaluating because it decouples Hub power from the very PSU being monitored. USB is an acceptable primary link for the workstation/regulated-desktop segment but is a frequent objection in racks (no lights-out access if the host is down, cable fragility, no remote OOB), which is exactly what MC's undefined "redundant uplinks" must answer with a network path. The differentiators CEC actually owns — per-rail DC-side granularity that no BMC/PDU can see, and the mezzanine integrated Hub+24-pin appliance as a single OEM-installable SKU — are real, but they only monetize once the table-stakes surfaces (class-driver USB enumeration, Redfish-aligned data model, Prometheus/SNMP export, mounting kits, signed fleet-deployable firmware) exist. The plan of record (PolarFire, TBD BOM, two deployment postures) already absorbs the BOM collision; this lens adds that ENT-NET is unsellable through integrators without the standard-Ethernet + monitoring-stack story, and ENT-AIR without a fully-local export path.

expectations.item: Standard 1000BASE-T RJ-45 uplink (IEEE 802.3ab) on the networked enterprise variant, with magnetics and port over-voltage/ESD protection
expectations.why: Enterprise/data-center switching is universally 1000BASE-T; 1000BASE-T1 is an automotive/industrial single-pair PHY (~15 m UTP) with no ports on enterprise switches, forcing media converters into every deployment

expectations.item: Driverless host attach: enumerate as a USB class device (CDC-ACM or WinUSB via Microsoft OS descriptors) needing no third-party kernel driver on Windows 10+/mainline Linux; any shipped driver package WHQL-signed
expectations.why: Enterprise IT will not deploy unsigned or custom kernel drivers; Microsoft has required WHQL signing for kernel drivers since 2021, while class devices sidestep the problem entirely (cdc-acm is mainline in Linux)

expectations.item: Documented host API + data formats: local REST/gRPC API with versioned schema, Prometheus exporter, SNMPv3 MIB, syslog/CEF event output, data model aligned to DMTF Redfish Sensor/PowerSubsystem schemas
expectations.why: Integrators buy telemetry hardware to feed existing stacks (Prometheus/Grafana, DCIM via SNMP, SIEM via syslog, Redfish tooling); a device with no documented machine-readable surface cannot be integrated at fleet scale

expectations.item: Coexistence/complement story vs BMC (IPMI/Redfish) telemetry that servers already carry
expectations.why: Every enterprise server already reports PSU-level power via its BMC; CEC must position per-rail DC-side (EPS/PCIe/12VHPWR) telemetry as the granularity the BMC cannot see, and export it into the same Redfish/Prometheus pipelines rather than a parallel silo

expectations.item: Defined mechanical mounting SKUs: PCI slot bracket, 2.5"/3.5" drive-bay tray, chassis standoff/magnetic mounts for the Hub; max component height + airflow guidance so modules qualify in 1U/2U and dense workstation chassis
expectations.why: Per-rail interposers physically sit in the PSU cable path near GPUs/CPU VRMs; OEMs cannot ship zip-tied floating boards, and integrators need repeatable install instructions and service-manual-grade mechanical drawings

expectations.item: Cable management program for the module fan-out: fixed-length low-profile Cat5e/Cat6 SKUs with right-angle boots, routing guidance, airflow-blockage limits (resolves OQ-4 for these tiers)
expectations.why: An 8-port Hub plus 4-6 interposers adds 4-8 internal RJ-45 runs plus the bridging cables; in a 1U/2U or SFF workstation that is the first thing an OEM thermal/service review rejects

expectations.item: Internal USB 2.0 motherboard-header attach option (9-pin/19-pin header cable) in addition to the external USB port
expectations.why: OEM system builders and rack integrators prefer permanent internal devices on internal headers — no external cable to knock loose, no occupied external port, cleaner chassis-closed qualification

expectations.item: Fleet-deployable signed firmware updates: host-agent or network-driven update packaged for Intune/SCCM/Ansible, never a GUI-only or press-BOOT-button flow; signed images with anti-rollback
expectations.why: Enterprises manage thousands of endpoints; a telemetry device that needs hands-on reflashing is a support liability, and the secure-boot/MCUboot direction in Appendix B.3 already points here

expectations.item: White-label/ODM program: OEM VID/PID and branding config, configurable LED behavior, co-brandable enclosure/silk, PCN discipline, 5+ year supply and firmware-support commitment
expectations.why: The realistic enterprise channel is system integrators and workstation/server OEMs bundling CEC, and ODM buyers contractually require branding hooks, change notification, and lifecycle guarantees

expectations.item: Mezzanine integrated Hub+24-pin appliance as an orderable single SKU
expectations.why: One board stack, one install step, two fewer cables — exactly the form OEMs want to drop into a build line; strong differentiator vs selling a bag of boards and patch cables

expectations.item: In-chassis environmental spec: operating ambient to at least 55°C with directed airflow, vibration tolerance, Class A EMC
expectations.why: Inside a loaded server chassis local ambient runs 40-55°C; the current spec's thermal work (§6.6) is about shunt self-heating, not a declared environmental envelope an OEM can qualify against

expectations.item: Fully-local operation for the air-gapped variant: all telemetry, APIs, and the Appendix D support pipeline function with zero cloud egress (on-prem swarm or export-to-media)
expectations.why: ENT-AIR customers (the owner's own variant framing) prohibit egress by definition; any feature that silently degrades without cloud is a disqualifier in that segment

integrations.protocol: HTTP /metrics (OpenMetrics)
integrations.requirement: Host agent (and the ENT-NET Hub itself over its Ethernet uplink) exposes a Prometheus exporter with stable, documented metric names for per-rail V/I/P/energy, transient events, and module inventory

integrations.system: DMTF Redfish ecosystem (BMC-adjacent tooling, DGX/Supermicro-class fleet managers)
integrations.protocol: Redfish REST (JSON, Sensor/PowerSubsystem/TelemetryService schemas)
integrations.requirement: Model CEC telemetry on Redfish schema types and expose a Redfish-style service (host agent on ENT, natively on the ENT-NET Hub) so fleet tools ingest CEC alongside BMC data; document the per-rail granularity as complementary to BMC PSU-level readings

integrations.system: DCIM / NMS platforms (Nagios, Zabbix, LibreNMS, DCIM suites)
integrations.protocol: SNMPv3
integrations.requirement: Publish a CEC enterprise MIB (per-rail sensors, module presence/DETECT state, Hub health, traps for transient/threshold events); SNMP applies because it is the DCIM lingua franca — facility-side Modbus/BACnet do NOT apply and should be explicitly declined

integrations.protocol: syslog (RFC 5424) / CEF
integrations.requirement: Structured event output for module hot-plug, threshold/transient events, firmware updates, and (Appendix D) signed-plan executions with consent records

integrations.protocol: USB CDC-ACM or WinUSB w/ MS OS 2.0 descriptors; MSI/Intune
integrations.requirement: Enumerate with in-box class drivers (no custom kernel driver; WHQL only if a driver package is unavoidable); host agent shipped as silent-installable MSI, manageable by Intune/SCCM/GPO

integrations.protocol: cdc-acm tty / hidraw + udev; .deb/.rpm
integrations.requirement: Mainline-driver enumeration, shipped udev rules and systemd-packaged agent in signed distro-native packages; document SELinux contexts for regulated builds

integrations.protocol: CLI + JSON output, REST API
integrations.requirement: Every provisioning/firmware/config action scriptable headlessly with machine-readable exit states — required for integrator factory provisioning lines

integrations.protocol: REST webhooks / API
integrations.requirement: Appendix D support-pipeline stages (ticket, consent, signed-plan execution, verification, sign-off label) must be mirrorable into the customer's ITSM as change records, or enterprises cannot authorize automated remediation

integrations.protocol: NTP (host-mediated) / PTP on the ENT-NET uplink
integrations.requirement: Timestamp discipline so per-rail events correlate across a fleet and against BMC/SEL logs; the Appendix B TSN/PTP leaning should surface as a concrete timestamping requirement, not just fabric capability

integrations.protocol: IEEE 802.3ab 1000BASE-T (recommended) vs 802.3bp 1000BASE-T1 (current spec)
integrations.requirement: If T1 is retained, CEC must supply and support media converters and document the 15 m reach limit; the integration-clean answer is a standard 1000BASE-T PHY + magnetics + RJ-45 with the OQ-14 over-voltage network on that port

gaps.gap: No host-side software surface is defined anywhere for either tier: no driver posture, no API, no data schema, no monitoring-stack integration (Redfish/Prometheus/SNMP/syslog). The §6 register map in the plan has slots for hardware but only 'diagnostics & support-pipeline hooks' on the software side.

1000BASE-T1 as the named uplink: an automotive/industrial single-pair PHY with ~15 m reach and no enterprise switch ecosystem — every real deployment needs media converters. For an integrator-sold ENT-NET product this kills the network story as specced.

No mechanical/mounting specification for Hub or modules inside a chassis (brackets, trays, standoffs, max heights, service clearances), and no cable-management program for the multi-RJ-45 + interposer fan-out (OQ-4 unresolved). OEM design-in reviews fail on exactly this.

USB as the primary host link is unexamined for the rack/server context: host-down means telemetry-path-down, no lights-out access, and the device shares fate with the OS it may be diagnosing. MC's 'redundant uplinks' is a bare phrase with no defined media, failover semantics, or independence claim.

Hub power is specced as 5VSB from the monitored PSU (§2.7 LOCKED): the telemetry system dies with the PSU it exists to observe. §2.9's wall-wart/NanoKVM third source is PROPOSED but not bound into the MC 'redundant power' requirement; MC needs an independent-feed requirement with defined ride-through.

No BMC/Redfish coexistence positioning: enterprise buyers will ask 'my iDRAC/iLO already shows power — why this?' and 'does it feed my existing dashboards?'. The per-rail differentiation argument and the export path both need to be written down as requirements.

RJ-11 'trust channel' is named with zero definition (what it carries, why RJ-11, isolation). In an IT environment RJ-11 invites mis-plugging into telephone/analog lines and has no rack ecosystem; integrators will push back on a nonstandard console-adjacent port without a spec.

No environmental envelope for in-chassis operation (operating ambient, airflow dependency, vibration) and no EMC/compliance class declared for either tier; the plan's Phase-2 item 7 acknowledges this but the register slots must include OEM-qualifiable numbers.

No white-label/ODM program definition (branding hooks, OEM VID/PID, PCN/lifecycle commitments, supply assurance). Not needed for direct sales, but it is the price of admission to the integrator/OEM channel that these tiers implicitly target.

Mezzanine integrated-appliance form (the natural OEM SKU) exists only as a design draft + pending OQ; neither tier's summary references a product form at all (external box? internal board? enclosure?).

Firmware update mechanism for fleets is undefined at tier level (MCUboot/signed OTA is an Appendix B leaning only); no requirement yet that updates be silent, scriptable, and deployable via standard endpoint-management tooling.

$50/$80 BOM rows are incompatible with PolarFire + a real Ethernet uplink (PHY, magnetics, connector, OV protection) + secure element — already re-baselined to TBD by owner direction, but the stale rows still stand in spec §1/§9 and both READMEs until Phase 4.

req_candidates.statement: REQ-HUB-NET: The ENT-NET Hub SHALL provide a standard IEEE 802.3ab 1000BASE-T uplink on RJ-45 with integrated magnetics and port-level over-voltage/surge/ESD protection (closing the OQ-14 enterprise half on this port). 1000BASE-T1 MAY be offered only as a documented factory option for embedded/vehicle-adjacent integrations, never as the default enterprise uplink.

REQ-HUB-NET: Evaluate and decide (owner gate) IEEE 802.3af/at PoE powering of the ENT-NET Hub uplink, so Hub power can be independent of the monitored PSU; record the interaction with the LOCKED §2.7 5VSB feed as an explicit priority-OR extension per §2.9.

REQ-HUB-COMMON: The USB host link SHALL enumerate using in-box OS class drivers (CDC-ACM and/or vendor class via WinUSB + Microsoft OS 2.0 descriptors) on Windows 10+ and mainline Linux, requiring no third-party kernel driver; any optional driver package SHALL be WHQL-signed.

REQ-HUB-COMMON: The host software stack SHALL expose (a) a versioned local REST API with published JSON schema, (b) a Prometheus/OpenMetrics exporter, (c) an SNMPv3 agent with a published CEC MIB, and (d) RFC 5424 syslog event output; the telemetry data model SHALL be aligned to DMTF Redfish Sensor/PowerSubsystem schema semantics and the mapping published.

REQ-HUB-COMMON: Documentation SHALL state the BMC-coexistence position: CEC provides per-rail DC-side telemetry complementary to BMC/IPMI PSU-level reporting, and SHALL demonstrate ingestion of CEC data into at least one Redfish-consuming fleet tool and one Prometheus/Grafana stack as a verification (demonstration) item.

REQ-MECH-COMMON: CEC SHALL define and ship mounting kits for the Hub and each module family — minimum: PCI slot bracket, 2.5"/3.5" drive-bay tray, and standoff/adhesive-standoff chassis mounts — and SHALL publish maximum component heights, keep-out volumes, and airflow guidance sufficient for 2U (target) and 1U (stretch) qualification.

REQ-MECH-COMMON: CEC SHALL offer fixed-length internal cable SKUs (Cat5e/Cat6 with low-profile right-angle boots, plus the 24-pin bridging cable) in lengths resolving OQ-4 for in-chassis routing, with a documented routing/airflow-impact guide per chassis class (tower workstation, 2U, 1U).

REQ-HUB-ENT: The Hub SHALL support attachment via an internal USB 2.0 motherboard header (9-pin) cable as an alternative to the external USB port, so integrators can ship chassis-closed installations.

REQ-HUB-MC: 'Redundant uplinks' SHALL be defined as at least two independent host paths of different media (USB device link + 1000BASE-T network link) with documented failover semantics, independent buffering, and a stated telemetry-loss budget during failover; at least one path SHALL remain available with the host OS down.

REQ-HUB-MC: 'Redundant power' SHALL include at least one power source independent of the monitored PSU (per the §2.9 three-source priority-OR: main 5V, 5VSB, external/wall-wart or PoE), with a specified ride-through duration and persist-on-fault flush covering total system power loss.

REQ-FW-COMMON: Firmware updates SHALL be cryptographically signed with anti-rollback (MCUboot-class chain per Appendix B.3), deliverable headlessly via the host agent and via the network uplink (ENT-NET), packaged for standard endpoint-management deployment (MSI/Intune, deb/rpm/Ansible), with no interactive or physical-button step in the fleet path.

REQ-ENV-COMMON: The Hub and all modules SHALL specify an in-chassis operating envelope of 0-55°C local ambient with defined minimum airflow (or a derating curve), and EMC compliance SHALL be declared at FCC/CE Class A minimum for the enterprise variants.

REQ-PROG-ENT: An OEM/white-label program SHALL be defined covering: OEM USB VID/PID and descriptor branding, configurable LED behavior/branding, co-brandable documentation, product change notification (PCN) commitments, and a minimum 5-year supply + security-update window.

REQ-FORM-COMMON: The mezzanine Hub-on-24-pin integrated appliance SHALL be carried as an orderable product form for the enterprise variants (D-ENT-5 adopt), with the enterprise Hub rev retaining the mezzanine socket contract (connector reference + mount frame) defined in the 2026-06-24 stack design.

REQ-AIR-COMMON: On the ENT-AIR variant, all telemetry access, APIs, alerting, and any adopted Appendix D support-pipeline function SHALL operate with zero network egress (local-only APIs, export-to-removable-media evidence path, on-prem plan generation or none), verified by demonstration on an egress-blocked network.

REQ-TIME-COMMON: The Hub SHALL timestamp module events against a disciplined clock synchronized via the host (NTP-mediated) or, on ENT-NET, natively (NTP/PTP on the Ethernet uplink), with published accuracy bounds sufficient for cross-machine event correlation against BMC/SEL logs.

challenges: 1000BASE-T1 uplink (spec §1 Enterprise row): T1 is automotive/industrial single-pair Ethernet — ~15 m reach, no ports on any enterprise switch, media converters required everywhere. Integrators will demand standard 1000BASE-T RJ-45; the Phase-2 research item 2 should be re-scoped from 'T1 PHY candidates' to 'standard-T-first, T1-optional', and OQ-14's enterprise over-voltage answer attaches to whichever port ships.

USB as the primary host link: fine for the workstation/regulated-desktop segment CEC grew from, but a frequent objection in racks — host-down = telemetry-down, no lights-out access, shared fate with the OS being diagnosed. MC's undefined 'redundant uplinks' must resolve this with an OS-independent network path, or the MC tier is a workstation product wearing a server label.

BOM targets $50/$80: collide with PolarFire SoC + GbE PHY/magnetics + secure element + mounting/enclosure — already re-baselined to TBD by owner direction (D-ENT-3), but spec §1/§9 and both hub READMEs still carry the stale rows; an OEM-channel product also needs margin stacking (distributor + integrator), which pushes realistic BOM discipline harder than direct-sale pricing.

LOCKED §2.7 Hub-powered-from-monitored-5VSB: for MC this is a structural conflict — the instrument shares its power source with its subject. The §2.9 proposed third source (wall-wart/NanoKVM) or PoE must graduate from PROPOSED to a binding MC redundant-power requirement.

Tier-agnostic modules (LOCKED §1/§8) vs OEM/air-gap reality: ESP32-S3/C6 modules are radio-capable silicon, and OEM/ENT-AIR customers commonly prohibit RF-capable parts outright — already flagged in the plan §1a.5; additionally, OEM design-in of interposers inserts extra mated connector pairs into EPS/PCIe/12VHPWR power paths, which OEM reliability teams will qualify skeptically and which the 12VHPWR board-mount-plus-pigtail rationale (§2.8) should be generalized into an OEM-facing reliability argument.

RJ-11 trust channel: a nonstandard, undefined port in an IT environment with mis-plug risk into analog phone/PoE wiring; if the trust function survives Phase-2 research it likely belongs on USB, the Ethernet uplink, or a keyed non-RJ connector — the RJ-11 choice itself should be treated as open, not inherited.

Appendix D support pipeline as cloud-shaped: stages 1/3/8 (in-app paid request, off-machine swarm, corpus write) assume egress and per-incident consumer payment; enterprise procurement buys support contracts, requires ITSM change-record integration, and ENT-AIR forbids the egress entirely — the pipeline needs an enterprise deployment profile (on-prem swarm or disabled actuation) before it can appear in either tier's requirements.

The mezzanine stack is currently framed as a Standard-tier packaging convenience; for OEM it is arguably the flagship enterprise form factor (one SKU, one install step) — the enterprise Hub rev should be required to honor the mezzanine alignment contract rather than treating it as an optional afterthought.
