result.summary: No incumbent ships what CEC's Enterprise/MC tiers aim at: fleet-deployable, vendor-agnostic, DC-side per-rail telemetry inside the machine with sub-ms 12VHPWR per-pin transient forensics plus an out-of-band (NanoKVM) vantage. The adjacent markets are commoditized on other axes — smart PDUs own AC-side per-outlet metering with billing-grade ±1% accuracy and SNMP/Redfish/DCIM integration; PMBus PSU telemetry via BMC/Redfish is table stakes in every server but is 100ms-1s averaged with no cable/pin visibility; NVIDIA PCAT is reviewer-only (3 rails, 100ms), nvidia-smi is documented as unreliable for power, and Powenetics v2 is a lab rig, not a hardened fleet product. Consumer per-pin monitoring (ASUS ROG Astral's IT8915FN, Corsair PinProtect+) validates the melting-connector pain but is single-SKU/single-vendor and not audit-grade — CEC's per-pin, PSU-and-GPU-agnostic forensics is a genuine differentiator, and AI-datacenter power-transient research shows enterprise demand for exactly this sub-100ms DC-side visibility. However, the current tier definitions miss nearly all enterprise TABLE STAKES: there is no standards-based northbound interface anywhere in the spec (zero mentions of Redfish/SNMP/IPMI/PMBus), the optional uplink is 1000BASE-T1 automotive single-pair rather than standard Ethernet, there is no accuracy/calibration traceability program, no FIPS/validation path for the named "secure element"/"crypto", and no fleet identity/provenance stronger than DETECT+MAC. Pricing implication: comparable enterprise power-visibility gear (metered/switched PDUs, OOB appliances) sells at $1k-3k/unit, so the superseded $50/$80 BOM anchors were the wrong frame — price on forensic value; the PolarFire direction is competitively justified because transient capture in fabric is the moat no PMBus/PDU product can follow.

expectations.item: Standards-based northbound management interface (Redfish REST/JSON and/or SNMPv3, HTTPS API) consumable by DCIM and observability stacks
expectations.why: Every enterprise power-visibility product — smart PDUs (Raritan, ServerTech, APC) and server PSU telemetry via OpenBMC — exposes SNMPv3/Redfish; DCIM integration is the stated deployment requirement for PMBus-enabled PSUs. A telemetry appliance that cannot be scraped by the customer's existing tooling is a lab instrument, not an enterprise product.

expectations.item: Standard Ethernet management port (1000BASE-T RJ-45 or SFP), out-of-band from the monitored host
expectations.why: PDUs, BMCs, and OOB consoles all present standard Ethernet; the BMC pattern (no agent on the production host) is the expected posture in datacenters. USB-to-host-agent as the only path is a consumer pattern.

expectations.item: Stated metering accuracy class with per-unit factory calibration and traceability
expectations.why: Billing-grade PDUs advertise ±1% per IEC 62053-21; PMBus PSU controllers publish accuracy specs. Enterprise buyers ask 'accurate to what, proven how' — CEC has good raw numbers (±0.3-1%) but no calibration/traceability story.

expectations.item: Validated cryptography and signed firmware chain (FIPS 140-3/CMVP path, secure boot, SBOM, supply-chain provenance)
expectations.why: The spec's own Enterprise target market is 'Regulated / financial'; FIPS 140-3 certificates are demanded across the supply chain in federal/regulated procurement, and OOB-management vendors (ZPE etc.) lead with it.

expectations.item: Alerting with configurable thresholds, historical retention, and event export (syslog/SIEM, webhook)
expectations.why: Baseline capability of every monitored PDU and DCIM feed; regulated-finance buyers additionally require security/audit events in their SIEM.

expectations.item: Fleet manageability: bulk provisioning, per-unit hardware identity, firmware update at scale, inventory reporting
expectations.why: Enterprise deploys tens-to-thousands of units; PDU vendors ship fleet managers. CEC's OQ-44 enumeration inventory is the seed but identity today is factory-MAC+database (weak).

expectations.item: Redundant power feeds and redundant management uplinks with defined failover semantics (MC tier)
expectations.why: Dual-feed is the norm for anything labeled mission-critical in a rack (dual-corded PDUs, dual BMC NICs); the MC summary row names redundancy but defines nothing.

expectations.item: Sub-ms per-rail DC-side transient capture with pre-trigger ring buffer, fleet-deployable
expectations.why: PMBus/BMC telemetry is 100ms-1s averaged and PSU readings 'systematically overestimate' — AI-datacenter power-stabilization literature (Microsoft/OpenAI arXiv 2508.14318, EasyRider) documents multi-kW ms-scale swings nobody can see per-node. Nobody ships this as a hardened fleet product; PCAT (100ms, reviewer-only) and Powenetics (lab rig) don't count.

expectations.item: Vendor-agnostic per-pin 12VHPWR/12V-2x6 forensics (detect pin-hog/loose-contact before melt, evidence-grade capture)
expectations.why: ASUS Astral's per-pin sensing (only one GPU SKU) and Corsair PinProtect+ (only Corsair PSUs+cables) prove market demand from the 4090/5090 melting saga; CEC is the only architecture that does it inline, for ANY GPU and ANY PSU, with a pre-roll buffer — an insurance/RMA-forensics wedge no incumbent matches.

expectations.item: Out-of-band visual + electrical fusion (NanoKVM vantage) and dead-system forensic extraction
expectations.why: Correlating electrical events with screen state/stop codes and extracting flash data from a dead system without opening the case has no competitive counterpart; nearest analogues (PiKVM, BMC KVM) do video only, no electrical fusion.

expectations.item: Air-gapped deployment posture (no RF silicon, no egress, local export only)
expectations.why: Classified/defense and some financial environments prohibit radio-capable parts and require one-way/offline telemetry export; almost no COTS monitoring vendor serves this well — a defensible niche for ENT-AIR if the module radio question is solved.

integrations.system: DCIM platforms (Sunbird, Nlyte, EcoStruxure) and NMS
integrations.protocol: SNMPv3 (custom MIB) and/or Redfish REST/JSON
integrations.requirement: CEC Enterprise Hub must expose an SNMPv3 agent or Redfish service (PowerSubsystem/Sensor-shaped schema) over a standard Ethernet management port so per-rail/per-cable telemetry lands in the customer's existing power dashboards; today the spec specifies no northbound protocol at all.

integrations.protocol: OpenMetrics/HTTP exporter (or documented host-app exporter)
integrations.requirement: A first-party metrics endpoint or exporter; the community already built a Grafana dashboard for Corsair HXi PSUs — enterprise expects this out of the box, versioned and supported.

integrations.protocol: Redfish aggregation or documented sensor-complement positioning
integrations.requirement: CEC must define how its DC-side data coexists with the BMC's PMBus PSU telemetry (complement, not conflict): either register as a Redfish aggregated device or document correlation keys (timestamps, rail names) so operators can join the two views.

integrations.protocol: syslog/CEF or JSON event stream, signed audit records
integrations.requirement: Security-relevant events (firmware update, support-pipeline signed-plan execution per Appendix D, trust-channel actions, tamper) must export as attributable, tamper-evident audit records — regulated-finance table stakes.

integrations.protocol: NTP (PTP for MC/forensic grade)
integrations.requirement: Transient forensic captures are only evidence if timestamps correlate with host logs, BMC logs, and facility power events; the Hub needs a disciplined clock and a stated correlation accuracy (~±1ms class). Nothing in the spec addresses time sync.

integrations.system: Host GPU tooling (nvidia-smi/DCGM, GPU Tweak-class vendor tools)
integrations.protocol: Host-app correlation layer (Concierge), read-only APIs
integrations.requirement: The Concierge/host app should ingest nvidia-smi/DCGM counters to fuse software-reported vs measured power — the arXiv 'Part-time Power Measurements' critique of nvidia-smi is CEC's best sales exhibit and needs the integration to demonstrate it.

gaps.gap: No northbound management/integration interface is specified anywhere: the spec has zero occurrences of Redfish, SNMP, IPMI, or PMBus, and the host link is USB to a host app. Enterprise buyers cannot deploy a monitoring appliance their DCIM/NMS cannot talk to.

The optional uplink is 1000BASE-T1 — automotive single-pair Ethernet. Enterprise racks and offices run standard 1000BASE-T/SFP; a T1 port requires media converters nobody stocks. The uplink PHY choice does not match any target customer environment.

No accuracy class, calibration procedure, or per-unit traceability program. Competing claims are concrete (PDU ±1% IEC 62053-21, PMBus controller datasheet specs); CEC's ±0.3-1% figures are design numbers with no verification/calibration story an enterprise procurement can cite.

'Secure element' / 'crypto' are named with no validation path (FIPS 140-3/CMVP, secure boot chain, SBOM). For the spec's own 'Regulated / financial' Enterprise market this is a procurement gate; for federal/defense (the natural ENT-AIR buyer) it is a hard blocker.

Module identity is DETECT resistor + factory MAC + database — no per-module hard identity or provenance (the §2.3 1-Wire ID/EEPROM path exists but is explicitly NOT adopted). Supply-chain provenance and anti-counterfeit expectations in regulated fleets exceed this; OQ-44 acknowledges it but nothing resolves it for the tiers that need it.

No fleet-management definition: provisioning N hubs, bulk firmware update, central inventory, RBAC on the management plane. Every enterprise PDU/OOB vendor ships this; the spec is silent above single-Hub scope.

No time-synchronization requirement, so transient forensic captures cannot be correlated to host/BMC/facility logs — undermining the forensics differentiator itself in any multi-system incident investigation.

MC 'redundant uplinks / redundant power / redundant CAN' are words in a table row with no failover semantics, detection times, or degrade ladder — competitors define dual-feed transfer behavior precisely; an MC buyer will ask in the first meeting.

RJ-11 'trust channel' has no counterpart in any competing product or customer environment; undefined purpose plus a nonstandard jack invites objection rather than differentiation until it is specified with a threat model.

ENT-AIR module problem: all module MCUs (ESP32-S3/C6) are radio-capable silicon, which air-gapped/classified buyers commonly prohibit outright — already flagged in the plan (§1a.5) but unresolved, and it collides with the LOCKED tier-agnostic-modules principle.

No packaging/positioning of the per-pin 12VHPWR forensic capture as an evidence product (export format, retention, chain-of-custody) — the one capability no competitor has is currently only an electrical feature, not a sellable forensic workflow.

req_candidates.statement: REQ-HUB-NET: The ENT-NET Hub SHALL provide a dedicated out-of-band management port using standard Ethernet (1000BASE-T RJ-45 and/or SFP), electrically isolated from the monitored host, exposing all telemetry and configuration without requiring any agent on the monitored machine.

REQ-HUB-COMMON: The Hub SHALL expose a documented, versioned northbound API in at least one datacenter-standard form (Redfish REST/JSON service and/or SNMPv3 with a published MIB), plus an OpenMetrics endpoint, sufficient for DCIM and Prometheus-class integration of all per-rail, per-cable, and per-pin channels.

REQ-HUB-COMMON: Every current/power channel SHALL carry a stated accuracy class verified by per-unit factory calibration with retained calibration records; system-level current/power accuracy SHALL be ≤±1% (target ±0.5%) with the verification method (test) defined in the register.

REQ-HUB-COMMON: The cryptographic subsystem (plan signing per Appendix D, firmware signing, identity) SHALL use a FIPS 140-3 validated module or one on a committed CMVP path; firmware SHALL be secure-boot chained and shipped with an SBOM.

REQ-HUB-COMMON: The Hub SHALL discipline its clock from customer NTP (PTP optional for MC) and timestamp all transient/forensic events such that they correlate to external logs within a stated bound (≤±1 ms with PTP, ≤±10 ms with NTP).

REQ-HUB-COMMON: Transient forensic captures (per-pin 12VHPWR, §6.13 EPS/PCIe events) SHALL be exportable in a documented, integrity-protected (signed/hashed) format with pre-trigger context, suitable for RMA disputes and incident review, retrievable both via the management API and via the out-of-band/dead-system path.

REQ-HUB-COMMON: Security-relevant events (auth, config change, firmware update, Appendix-D plan execution, tamper) SHALL emit attributable audit records exportable to customer SIEM via syslog/CEF or a JSON stream.

REQ-FLEET-COMMON: Enterprise/MC deployments SHALL support fleet operation: per-Hub unique cryptographic identity (secure-element anchored), bulk provisioning and firmware update, role-based access on the management plane, and a module inventory report at enumeration (closes the OQ-44 shape for these tiers).

REQ-HUB-MC: The MC Hub SHALL provide dual power feeds through a hardware prioritizer (LTC4417-class) and dual management uplinks with automatic failover; failover detection time, telemetry-loss budget during transfer, and the degrade ladder SHALL be specified and test-verified.

REQ-AIR: The ENT-AIR variant SHALL contain no operable RF transmitter: hub compute radio-free by construction (PolarFire), and the module radio question (radio-free MCU variant vs certified fused-off/antenna-absent ESP32 posture) resolved by explicit owner gate D-ENT-5 with customer-acceptable evidence, never assumed.

REQ-HUB-ENT: The RJ-11 trust channel SHALL either be specified with a concrete threat model, protocol, and customer-facing function before Phase 4, or be dropped from the Enterprise definition; an undefined nonstandard port is a net negative in enterprise evaluation.

challenges: 1000BASE-T1 is the wrong uplink PHY: it is automotive single-pair Ethernet, absent from datacenter/office infrastructure. Every competing enterprise device (PDU, BMC, OOB console) presents standard 1000BASE-T or SFP. The optional-T1 line in the §1 table should be re-baselined to standard Ethernet in the Phase-4 spec revision.

USB-as-primary-host-link is a consumer posture at these tiers: enterprise expects the BMC pattern — out-of-band network management with no agent on the production host. USB should demote to a provisioning/debug path on ENT-NET; on ENT-AIR the local path is the product, which is coherent.

The superseded $50/$80 BOM targets were the wrong frame competitively (owner has already TBD'd them — this lens reinforces): metered/switched PDUs sell for $1k-3k, OOB appliances similar, PCAT is not even purchasable, and no product on the market delivers CEC's capability. Price on forensic/fleet value; the Phase-2 costing should target function (PolarFire + standard Ethernet + validated crypto + calibration), and unit prices of $500-2500 are defensible.

The tier-agnostic-modules LOCKED principle collides with two enterprise realities surfaced by this lens: (a) radio-capable ESP32 module silicon in air-gapped environments, (b) weak DETECT+MAC module identity vs supply-chain provenance expectations (the not-adopted §2.3 1-Wire/EEPROM path). Both need explicit owner gates (already D-ENT-5 shaped), not quiet inheritance.

Classical CAN 500k (LOCKED) is adequate for telemetry rates but the Enterprise fleet-scale saturation question the spec itself scopes to OQ-7 becomes real if per-pin transient event bursts from 8+ modules ride CAN; the RS-485 streaming plane and the FPGA data plane must be sized so the LOCKED CAN floor is never the transient-forensics bottleneck.

The consumer flank is closing on the per-pin differentiator: ASUS Astral ships per-pin 12V-2x6 sensing today and Corsair PinProtect+ does per-pin OCP on its own cables. CEC's defensible position is vendor-agnostic + inline + pre-roll capture + fleet/audit-grade — the requirements must lock those four properties, because 'per-pin monitoring' alone will be table stakes on premium GPUs within a product cycle.

The RJ-11 trust channel and the mezzanine appliance form need competitive justification: no market counterpart exists for either. The mezzanine (integrated appliance) is actually the strongest enterprise packaging answer (one SKU, one install) and deserves promotion in the Enterprise product form discussion; the RJ-11 channel is the opposite — undefined and objection-prone.

drops.claim: Gap: "$50/$80 BOM targets are unreconciled with what this lens demands ... D-ENT-2/D-ENT-3 collision, worse under the PolarFire leaning" (severity major)
drops.reason: Stale against the plan of record it was told to read: docs/enterprise-mc-requirements-plan-2026-07-01.md §1a.3 + D-ENT-3 record the owner superseding the $50/$80 rows (BOM targets TBD, re-baselined by Phase-2 costing), and the PolarFire-vs-BOM collision is already the plan's own §7 standing risk. D-ENT-2 is not a 'leaning' — it is RESOLVED to PolarFire by owner direction. Nothing here is a gap the program lacks; it duplicates already-tracked plan state.

drops.claim: Gap: "No stated DCIM/asset-management export ... even though all the underlying data exists" (minor)
drops.reason: Duplicative: the same item appears as expectation 7 (per-module fleet inventory), req_candidate 10 (Redfish inventory + machine-readable export), and is subsumed by the 'no northbound data model' blocker gap. Three statements of one finding; the gap adds nothing the REQ does not.

revisions.claim: All "tier: both" network-management requirements (dedicated 802.3 management port, agentless-over-network, SNMPv3, NTP, syslog-over-TLS) and the blocker "primary Enterprise link is USB HS with network only optional"
revisions.fix: Re-scope to the owner's 2026-07-01 two-variant framing (plan §1a.2), which the audit never absorbed: ENT-AIR is defined as "no network egress by design; local/out-of-band only", so a mandatory network management port / Redfish / SNMP / NTP / syslog stack directly contradicts that variant's design intent. Scope the network-attached REQ set to ENT-NET (or make it VARIANT=NET conditional per the plan's REQ-<UNIT>-<VARIANT> schema); give ENT-AIR a distinct local/OOB export + offline-update requirement instead. The USB-primary finding stays a blocker for ENT-NET only; for ENT-AIR, host-independent LOCAL delivery (not network delivery) is the correct requirement. Note D-ENT-6: ENT-AIR may map to the Mission Critical label, in which case the MC "two network management uplinks" REQ as drafted could contradict an air-gapped MC — the redundant-uplink REQ must be posture-conditional too.

revisions.claim: Gap: "No security-management surface: ... no requirements for TLS cert enrollment, account/RBAC model, audit logging, syslog forwarding, or signed-firmware/anti-rollback workflow"
revisions.fix: Narrow it: spec Appendix B.3/B.5 already name TLS (mbedTLS/wolfSSL with FIPS-validated builds), MCUboot signed OTA, secure boot, attestation, and PUF-protected key storage, and plan Phase-2 research item 6 explicitly schedules hardening that stack into requirements — signed firmware is not absent, it is un-ratified. The genuinely missing items are: customer-CA certificate enrollment, an account/RBAC model, audit-event forwarding (syslog), and an explicit anti-rollback statement. Keep severity major for those four only, and position the REQ as feeding Phase-2 item 6 + the §6 'firmware/boot/OTA security' slot.

revisions.claim: Gap: "Appendix D support pipeline assumes an off-machine swarm with no stated on-prem/air-gapped deployment mode"
revisions.fix: Overstated: the spec already carries a no-cloud stance (OQ-45 telemetry residency), the service layer above the host is explicitly "CEC-hosted or self-hosted" (Appendix C.1), and OQ-66 records the swarm-internal ladder as "self-hosted worker tiers, then frontier models, then the human backstop". Revise to: self-hosted deployment is contemplated but not bound as a requirement for the regulated/defense segments, and the frontier-model rung of the OQ-66 ladder has no air-gap answer — the REQ should bind an on-prem-only pipeline mode (frontier rung disabled or replaced) plus customer-controlled OQ-62 signing roots. Severity drops to major-but-narrower (a binding gap, not an absence).

revisions.claim: Challenge: "...100BASE-TX on the ESP32-P4's native EMAC ... offering a cost-honest middle path that also weakens the PolarFire-for-Enterprise argument (Appendix B.5 / D-ENT-2)"
revisions.fix: Strip the PolarFire arbitration — D-ENT-2 is RESOLVED to PolarFire by recorded owner direction (plan §1a.1); the audit is re-litigating a closed decision. Keep the surviving, still-useful half: aggregate CEC telemetry (CAN 500k + a few ~1 MB/s RS-485 streams) fits comfortably in 100 Mbit, so gigabit is not a functional requirement — feed that as sizing input to the Phase-2 PolarFire part-selection/costing survey (the MPFS parts carry their own 10/100/1000 MACs, so the standard-Ethernet cost delta is mostly PHY+magnetics+jack, further weakening any cost objection to standard 802.3). The ESP32-P4 EMAC fact is verified true but now applies only if a P4-based fallback ever returns.

revisions.claim: REQ: "1000BASE-T1 SHALL NOT be the sole or default network uplink and may be retained only as an internal/inter-board link"
revisions.fix: Correct in thrust (verified: 1000BASE-T1 is automotive single-pair, no enterprise access switch terminates it, media converters are real per-node cost), but the wording must not collaterally ban the platform's separate, legitimate T1 use: 100BASE-T1 as the proposed Max-module streaming link on RJ-45 pair 2 (spec §2.3 DETECT 10k code, §6.11, OQ-20) is in-chassis module-side plumbing and out of this REQ's scope. Also do not delete Phase-2 research item 2 — reframe it to a standard-802.3 uplink survey, because it is where the deferred OQ-14 enterprise over-voltage protection answer lands regardless of PHY choice.

revisions.claim: Gap: "MC 'redundant uplinks' has no failover semantics" and Gap: "RJ-11 trust channel has no definition"
revisions.fix: Both grounded in the spec/READMEs (verified: the tier rows are the only specifying text), but present them as sharpening EXISTING plan slots rather than novel discoveries: Phase-2 research item 5 already targets "MC redundant CAN + redundant uplinks — failover semantics; transceiver/bus/port-level", and item 3 already targets the RJ-11 definition + threat model. The audit's real contribution is the concrete acceptance criteria (independent failure domains, failover eventing on both Redfish and SNMP paths; define-or-cut for RJ-11) — attach them to those research items.

revisions.claim: Gap: "No time-sync requirement (NTP/PTP)"
revisions.fix: Keep, with one grounding correction: Appendix B.3 already leans on PTP/TSN hardware timestamping in the data plane ("no general-purpose scheduler adding jitter under PTP and TSN"), so the hardware basis exists as a leaning — the gap is that nothing binds a time-sync REQUIREMENT or stamps it onto telemetry. The PTP-on-MC suggestion is consistent with, not additive to, the existing B.3/B.5 direction. Also scope the NTP-client REQ to ENT-NET; ENT-AIR needs a local time source (GNSS-free/manual/local NTP island) stated explicitly.

revisions.claim: Summary framing that the audit's requirements land against the "ESP32-P4 + secure element" Enterprise row and the P4-vs-PolarFire tension
revisions.fix: Update the frame: the plan of record supersedes the §1 tier row — Enterprise-class compute is PolarFire by owner direction (formal spec edit rides Phase 4), the ENT-AIR/ENT-NET variants are deployment postures, and enterprise module requirements are being drafted now (D-ENT-4 YES, amending the tier-agnostic principle via a Phase-4 owner-penned amendment). The audit's challenge 8 (1-Wire/module attestation as an explicit D-ENT-5 adopt/decline) is correctly aligned with the plan and should stand; everything else should cite the plan's D-gates and §6 slot names when proposing where its REQs live.

result.confidence: Trustworthiness is moderately high on external facts and low-to-moderate on repo currency. Every named standard, document number, product, and tool spot-checked is real and correctly characterized (DSP0266/2046/2056/0270, AggregationSource, Redfish-Service-Validator, ESP32-P4 10/100 EMAC, 1000BASE-T1 automotive PHY + media converters), and the core repo-grounded gaps (no northbound data model, RJ-11/redundancy undefined, §6 register map lacking a management-interface slot) verified against the spec and plan. The audit's systemic flaw is that it treated the 2026-07-01 owner direction as open questions: D-ENT-2 (PolarFire), D-ENT-3 (BOM TBD), D-ENT-4 (modules yes), and above all the ENT-AIR \"no network egress by design\" variant, which invalidates blanket network-attached requirements for that posture. Primary-source confirmation still needed: exact media-converter pricing class (~$300 is order-of-magnitude plausible, not verified), and whether ENT-AIR customers accept an isolated management LAN (which would partially restore the network REQ set for that variant) — an owner/customer-intake question, not a document one.

drops.claim: Challenge 4's architecture prescription: "an ordinary gigabit MAC+PHY on an RTOS with NTP is sufficient for Enterprise" (as an argument against the PolarFire compute choice)
drops.reason: Re-litigates D-ENT-2, which the owner RESOLVED to PolarFire by recorded direction on 2026-07-01 (docs/enterprise-mc-requirements-plan-2026-07-01.md §1a.1) — a document the audit itself lists in its sources. Arguing the compute plane back to a plain MCU/RTOS contradicts a recorded owner decision, the same class of violation as touching a LOCKED fact. The salvageable half of the challenge (DCIM ingestion needs no TSN; PTP scopes to MC/broadcast) survives as a revision below.

revisions.claim: Challenge 2 + Gap 1 + REQ-ENT network-plane candidates: "the 'optional' 1000BASE-T1 should become a mandatory Ethernet management port on Enterprise" (and the tier-wide SNMP/REST/DHCP/802.1X mandates)
revisions.fix: Condition every network-facing requirement on the ENT-NET variant. Owner direction (plan §1a.2) splits Enterprise into ENT-AIR (air-gapped, NO network egress by design) and ENT-NET (networked-hardened); a tier-wide mandatory Ethernet management port contradicts ENT-AIR outright. Rewrite as: ENT-NET SHALL provide the standard 10/100/1000BASE-T management plane (SNMP v3, REST/Redfish, syslog, NTP, 802.1X); ENT-AIR SHALL provide an out-of-band-equivalent local export path (USB/serial/removable, still UTC-stamped, audit-logged, threshold-capable). The underlying out-of-band monitoring point (5VSB host-independent operation) is grounded and stands.

revisions.claim: Challenge 1 + Gap 2: 1000BASE-T1 is automotive single-pair Ethernet, physically incompatible with enterprise 1000BASE-T switching (severity: blocker, tier: both)
revisions.fix: Substance VERIFIED (media-converter product ecosystem exists precisely for this gap). Keep, but correct scope and framing: (a) T1 is 'optional' and explicitly deferred to OQ-7 — nothing is locked or built, so this is a requirements-program blocker for ENT-NET, not a shipped-hardware defect; tier should be ENT-NET (+ MC pending D-ENT-6), not unconditional 'both'; (b) the concrete actionable output is to redirect the plan's Phase-2 research item 2 — currently a 1000BASE-T1-only PHY/magnetics survey — to a BASE-T-vs-T1 comparison, with OQ-14's enterprise over-voltage answer attaching to whichever uplink wins.

revisions.claim: Challenge 3: "The $50 Enterprise BOM target cannot cover... D-ENT-3 re-baseline is justified from this lens alone; ~$80 MC is even tighter"
revisions.fix: D-ENT-3 is ALREADY answered — owner direction (plan §1a.3) set BOM targets to TBD, superseding the $50/$80 rows, and the owner-directed PolarFire compute pushes cost further still. Reframe from 'the target must be re-baselined' (stale ask) to 'the managed-network-device feature set (PHY+magnetics, SE jobs, TLS/SNMPv3 stack, buffered-telemetry flash) is a costing input the Phase-2 D-ENT-3 re-baseline must include' — confirmatory evidence, not a new decision request.

revisions.claim: Challenge 4 (surviving half): PTP/fancy timestamping is relevant only to the MC broadcast vertical; DCIM ingestion is minute-class SNMP/REST polling
revisions.fix: Keep, reframed against the resolved compute choice: PolarFire is owner-decided, so the finding's correct form is a REQUIREMENTS constraint, not an architecture argument — Enterprise/ENT-NET requirements SHALL NOT derive TSN-switch data-plane obligations from Appendix B (DCIM polling + traps need only an ordinary MAC on the PolarFire); the IEEE 1588 PTP slave option scopes to the MC/broadcast (ST 2110) register only.

revisions.claim: Challenge 5 + Gap 10: "RJ-11 trust channel has no consumer... an undefined extra jack... define a concrete function and threat model or drop it; its value is zero"
revisions.fix: Partially stale: spec OQ-60 (§11.1 v3.11) already PROPOSES a concrete function — the trust/attestation role moves OFF the RJ-11 onto the secure element + a second CAN channel, and the jack is repurposed as the per-port Max power + bidirectional FREEZE-trigger companion connector (with the 'powered telco-shaped jack' foot-gun explicitly flagged). The plan's Phase-2 item 3 already schedules the definition + threat model. Keep the valid ops-lens core ('unexplained port fails enterprise security questionnaires' — a real input to that threat model, and OQ-60's proposal is PROPOSED, not ratified), but cite OQ-60 and drop the 'value is zero / undefined' wording.

revisions.claim: Expectation 5: declared accuracy class WITH per-unit factory calibration records, traceability, and drift/recalibration statement — table_stakes:true
revisions.fix: Split it. The published system-level accuracy spec benchmarked against the ±1% IEC 62053-21 billing-grade PDU norm is table stakes (Raritan benchmark VERIFIED, and the 'do not claim 62053 conformance for DC sensing' nuance is correct — keep that REQ language). But per-unit calibration records retrievable via the management plane EXCEEDS the PDU-market norm (Raritan/ServerTech certify model-level accuracy; they do not ship per-unit cal certs as a standard deliverable) — downgrade that half to SHOULD/differentiator, pending a customer whose regime (metrology/defense) demands it.

revisions.claim: REQ-MC: all cryptographic operations SHALL use a FIPS 140-3-validated crypto module — 'this constrains D-ENT-2's secure-element/PolarFire choice'
revisions.fix: Soften and update: D-ENT-2 is already resolved (PolarFire), so the requirement constrains PolarFire crypto-block/companion-SE selection, not an open architecture choice. Make FIPS validation a SHOULD/posture-target pending a named customer — consistent with the plan's own Phase-2 item 7 ('FIPS/CAVP?' is an open compliance-scan question, not a settled mandate).

revisions.claim: REQ-MC: failover SHALL raise a critical event 'within 1 s' on all alert channels
revisions.fix: The 1-second bound is unsourced (no PDU/DCIM norm cited and none exists at that specificity). Keep the observable-failover requirement — the 'redundancy an ops team cannot see is treated as absent' principle is sound and fills a real MC gap — but mark the latency figure as a placeholder for the plan's Phase-2 items 4-5 (MC redundant power/CAN research) to derive.

revisions.claim: Gap 9 + REQ-ENT fleet provisioning (DHCP bootstrap, zero-touch bulk config, staged firmware rollout)
revisions.fix: Keep for ENT-NET; add an ENT-AIR-conditional form (offline/media-based bulk provisioning and firmware update — air-gapped fleets still have hundreds of units but no DHCP/network path). As written it silently assumes the networked posture.

revisions.claim: Challenge 7: keep D-ENT-5 (1-Wire ID/EEPROM or SE-backed module-table attestation) alive as a customer-triggered option rather than declining it permanently
revisions.fix: Correct and grounded (§2.3 path confirmed not-adopted; tier-agnostic modules LOCKED and respected) — but note it CONFIRMS the existing plan rather than adding to it: D-ENT-5 already carries the 1-Wire/EEPROM path and module provenance participation as explicit Phase-3 owner line-items. Recast as endorsement with the dcim-ops rationale (authenticated hardware inventory ask from regulated fleets) attached as evidence.

revisions.claim: Challenge 8 + syslog REQ: Appendix D support-pipeline actions must export to SIEM/syslog and be fleet-wide disable-able by policy
revisions.fix: Keep — product-appropriate and well-timed (the plan's §6 register map already reserves a 'diagnostics & support-pipeline hooks (Appendix D)' slot this fills with concrete content). Add: ENT-AIR is effectively the hardware embodiment of the fleet-wide-disable posture (no egress = no remote actuation), which strengthens the two-variant framing rather than adding a new mechanism.

result.confidence: Trustworthy on substance: the two most load-bearing external claims (1000BASE-T1/1000BASE-T physical incompatibility; the ±1% IEC 62053-21 billing-grade PDU benchmark) were verified by web search, no hallucinated standards or products were found, and the core gap (zero SNMP/Redfish/syslog/NTP/kWh anywhere in the spec) was confirmed by direct grep. The lens result's one systemic defect is staleness against the 2026-07-01 owner direction in the plan-of-record it cites: it missed the ENT-AIR/ENT-NET two-variant split (so its tier-wide network mandates over-reach), the PolarFire resolution, and the already-TBD'd BOM targets — all fixed by the revisions above. Needing primary-source confirmation before ratification: DCIM vendor onboarding specifics (Power IQ dynamic-plugin format, Device42/EcoStruxure device-definition processes), whether real ENT-NET buyers demand 802.1X on an in-chassis telemetry accessory, and the actual Redfish schema mapping (no standard 'PowerRail' resource exists; the mapping needs a designed answer, not a name-drop).

drops.claim: Challenge 3 (D-ENT-2): '...the split option (Enterprise = P4+SE, MC = PolarFire) is the compliance-coherent one' and 'buying PolarFire for tier 3 breaks the $50 BOM'
drops.reason: Contradicts the recorded owner direction in the plan of record (docs/enterprise-mc-requirements-plan-2026-07-01.md §1a): D-ENT-2 is RESOLVED by owner direction to PolarFire for enterprise-class compute (both ENT-AIR and ENT-NET variants), and D-ENT-3 superseded the $50/$80 BOM rows (targets TBD, re-baselined by Phase-2 costing). The audit argues a decided gate from a dead cost constraint without flagging that it is challenging an owner decision. The verified ESP32-P4 security facts (Secure Boot v2, Key Manager/HUK, ECDSA peripheral — confirmed against Espressif docs) remain relevant to the MODULE MCUs and survive inside REQ-001/REQ-MC-SEC-013; the tier-3 architecture recommendation itself must go.

drops.claim: Gap 13: 'Powered RJ-11 mismate hazard (telco battery/ring voltages)... becomes moot if the trust channel is redefined' (tier: enterprise, minor)
drops.reason: Duplicative: the same mismate hazard already appears in challenge 1 (citing OQ-60(c)), in gap 4 (RJ-11 has no threat model), and is remediated inside REQ-ENT-SEC-014 ('with mismate protection'). Also a factual quibble: OQ-60's stated RJ-11 6P6C rationale is that it 'cannot mismate an RJ-45 jack' — the residual hazard is a telco cord into the CEC jack, which OQ-60(c) already owns as an open call. Nothing additive survives after the other three items.

revisions.claim: Whole-findings framing: Enterprise tier = 'ESP32-P4 + secure element' (summary, challenge 3, expectations, several REQs)
revisions.fix: Re-base the entire result on the plan-of-record §1a owner direction (2026-07-01): Enterprise-class compute is PolarFire SoC for BOTH deployment variants (ENT-AIR air-gapped, ENT-NET networked-hardened); the §1 table's P4+SE row is superseded pending the Phase-4 spec edit; BOM targets are TBD. Requirements should be written per-variant (AIR/NET/COMMON per the register schema), and the P4 security-silicon discussion should be repointed at the module MCUs (S3/C6), where it is still correct and load-bearing.

revisions.claim: Gap 1 / Challenge 2: 'No PSIRT/CVD/CRA readiness... ENISA reporting obligation lands 2026-09-11, before either tier's board even exists' (severity: blocker)
revisions.fix: Dates verified (reporting 2026-09-11, full essential requirements 2027-12-11), but the obligation binds manufacturers of products actually MADE AVAILABLE on the EU market — CEC currently has no product on the EU market and Enterprise/MC boards do not exist (Phase 5 unstarted). Recondition: 'blocker for any EU go-to-market, binding from first EU sale (and immediately if any Standard/Pro unit is already sold in the EU)' rather than an unconditional 10-week fire alarm. The platform-wide-floor point (security is not a tier-3 differentiator under CRA) stands and is the durable takeaway.

revisions.claim: REQ-ENT/MC-SEC-005: '...meet EU CRA Art. 14 reporting timelines (24h/72h/14d) via the ENISA platform'
revisions.fix: Correct the timeline: 24h early warning / 72h notification for both tracks, but the 14-day final report applies to actively exploited vulnerabilities; severe incidents allow 1 month. Also mark the '>= 5 years' support period as CEC's declared choice (CRA requires a support period reflecting expected product lifetime; 5 years is the customary reference, not a universal statutory minimum).

revisions.claim: REQ-ENT-SEC-008 / integrations: 'agent binaries SHALL be Authenticode/WHQL signed'
revisions.fix: WHQL certification applies to kernel-mode drivers, not application binaries. Revise to: user-mode Concierge/agent binaries Authenticode-signed with EV cert; WHQL/attestation signing required ONLY if the agent ships a kernel-mode component (current Appendix D L-profile collection is user-mode ETW/CIM/event-log — likely no driver needed, which is itself worth stating as a requirement: 'no kernel-mode component').

revisions.claim: Challenge 4 / REQ-ENT-SEC-009: 1000BASE-T1 uplink drags in 802.1X EAP-TLS + IDevID
revisions.fix: The coupling argument is sound and additive, but scope it: (a) per §1a, ENT-AIR has no network egress by design, so 802.1X/uplink requirements are ENT-NET-conditional only; (b) the plan's Phase-2 item 2 already surveys the T1 uplink + OQ-14 over-voltage — fold the supplicant/IDevID dependency into that existing research slot rather than a freestanding challenge; (c) soften 'no enterprise network speaks natively' — T1 media converters/SPE switches exist; the real point is that ANY Ethernet uplink on a controlled network triggers the NAC/certificate requirement.

revisions.claim: Challenge 7: Espressif (Shanghai) silicon supply-chain-origin objections for the Enterprise/MC tier
revisions.fix: With the owner's PolarFire (Microchip, US) direction the HUB concern largely dissolves; repoint the claim at the tier-agnostic MODULE MCUs (ESP32-S3/C6), and merge it with the plan's existing §1a.5 flag + Phase-2 item 8 (radio-free/alternative module MCU survey for ENT-AIR) so country-of-origin/HBOM is an added evaluation axis of that survey, not a new standalone position.

revisions.claim: Expectation/REQ-MC-SEC-011: IEC 62443-4-1 SDL + 62443-4-2 SL-2 self-assessment for MC
revisions.fix: Keep as non-table-stakes, but make it conditional on D-ENT-6 (the ENT-AIR/ENT-NET to tier-3/4 mapping is an open owner call) and on actually targeting OT/industrial buyers — 62443 is an IACS-component framework; for a PC/data-center telemetry accessory it is a customer-led evidence-pack posture, not a product-class obligation. Phase-2 item 7 (compliance regime scan) is the right home; cite it.

result.confidence: High on repo grounding: every spec citation I checked (OQ-44, OQ-60 incl. the trust-to-SE migration and the foot-gun open call, OQ-62, §2.3 1-Wire non-adoption, Appendix D's $25 in-app ticket and consent model) is accurate, and the audit respects the LOCKED facts (tier-agnostic modules, CAN 500k). External anchors verified by search: CRA dates (2026-09-11 / 2027-12-11) and ESP32-P4 security silicon; PolarFire security payload (PUF/DPA/Athena) and the 12-18-month CMVP queue are consistent with industry knowledge but were not primary-source-confirmed this pass. The one systemic defect is staleness against the 2026-07-01 owner direction (PolarFire decided, BOM TBD, two deployment variants) — after re-basing on that, the remaining challenges, gaps, and REQ candidates are sound and product-appropriate.

drops.claim: Challenge: "the ~$50 Enterprise BOM target is very unlikely to survive... either the target re-baselines or the fleet feature set decides between P4+SE (cheap, adequate for identity/OTA) and PolarFire (overkill for this lens)"
drops.reason: Stale against the plan of record the audit itself cites: docs/enterprise-mc-requirements-plan-2026-07-01.md §1a records owner direction (2026-07-01) that D-ENT-2 is RESOLVED to PolarFire and D-ENT-3 BOM targets are TBD ($50/$80 rows superseded). The P4-vs-PolarFire arbitration recommendation argues against a decided owner gate, and the target it says won't survive no longer exists. The surviving substance (PKI provisioning ceremony is a manufacturing-line cost; TLS/OTA A/B flash sizing) is moved to a revision.

drops.claim: Gap 1: "No fleet management plane exists at all in either tier definition: no provisioning flow, no device-management protocol, no monitoring integration, no config push, no inventory API" (severity: blocker)
drops.reason: Duplicative umbrella: every element is restated as its own gap (identity = gap 2, OTA = gap 3, monitoring/egress = gap 4, ZTP = gap 7, config-as-code appears in req candidates). Keeping it as a separate blocker double-counts severity; it belongs in the summary only. Also partially overstated as written: the plan's §6 register section map already reserves slots for identity & provenance, firmware/boot/OTA security, and diagnostics hooks, and Phase 2 items 6-7 cover the firmware/compliance halves — the true finding is that fleet OPERATIONS (provisioning, monitoring integration, inventory API, config push) has no register slot, which the itemized gaps already say.

revisions.claim: All findings framed against "ESP32-P4 + secure element" as the Enterprise compute/identity anchor (summary; gap 2 "the SE is a $2 part"; req candidate 1 "key generated or injected in the secure element"; integration row "factory-provision an IDevID keypair+cert in the Enterprise/MC secure element")
revisions.fix: Rebase on the recorded owner direction (plan §1a, 2026-07-01): Enterprise-class compute is PolarFire SoC (spec §1-table edit pending Phase 4). The identity findings survive intact but the anchor is the PolarFire root of trust (PUF-protected key storage, Athena crypto, DPA-resistant secure boot per Appendix B.3) — or a discrete SE only if Phase-2 costing brings one in. Reword req candidate 1 to "factory-provisioned 802.1AR IDevID with the private key held in the device root of trust (PolarFire PUF-protected storage per D-ENT-2, non-exportable)" and feed the IDevID/EST/attestation needs into Phase-2 research item 1 (PolarFire sizing vs OQ-44/62), where they materially help pick the MPFS part.

revisions.claim: Requirements and challenges asserted tier-blind or "both": EST/BRSKI enrollment, 802.1X uplink, hawkBit-class OTA client, Prometheus scrape "served directly from the network uplink", and challenge 2's "flip the default: uplink populated, USB the fallback"
revisions.fix: Condition per deployment variant per plan §1a/D-ENT-6: the program drafts ENT-NET (networked-but-hardened) vs ENT-AIR ("no network egress by design; local/out-of-band only"). The networked stack (EST/BRSKI+MASA, 802.1X/NAC, campaign-server OTA, scraped exporters, syslog/OTLP) is ENT-NET; ENT-AIR gets the offline halves the audit already names (local CA, sneakernet signed update bundles, local/OOB evidence egress) — and for ENT-AIR, USB/local-only egress is the intended posture, not a defect, so "uplink populated by default" applies to ENT-NET only. Note BRSKI's MASA requires manufacturer connectivity and is inapplicable to ENT-AIR (offline-voucher variants aside); EST is also NET-only.

revisions.claim: Gap 4 (blocker, both): "Telemetry-egress architecture is in-band and consumer-shaped... telemetry dies exactly when the machine does; and no Prometheus/OTel/syslog surface exists"
revisions.fix: Keep as blocker for ENT-NET (the monitoring-stack absence is real and is what the buyer evaluates), but re-scope the tier field: for ENT-AIR the Cloudflare-tunnel objection is vacuous (no egress by design) and host-independent evidence there rides the already-specified local OOB paths (§2.9 5VSB power, NanoKVM egress, persist-on-fault flash), which the audit's own non-table-stakes expectation 11 correctly credits. Also soften "USB device-control default-blocks": Defender/Ivanti-class device control is policy-configured, not on by default — the accurate claim is that managed fleets commonly require device/agent approval review, which the signed-enterprise-package requirement (last req candidate) already addresses.

revisions.claim: Gap 3 / CRA framing: "No fleet OTA story... The EU CRA makes the update+CVD+SBOM package legally mandatory for EU sale" (blocker, tier: both)
revisions.fix: Two corrections, neither fatal: (1) CRA obligations attach to every CEC product with digital elements sold in the EU — including the consumer Standard/Pro Hubs — so the CRA package is a platform-wide compliance program, not an Enterprise/MC tier differentiator; file it against Phase-2 research item 7 (compliance regime scan) with platform scope. (2) "No fleet OTA story" should acknowledge Phase-2 research item 6 already names MCUboot signed OTA + secure boot chain as a research slot and Appendix B.3 sketches it; the genuinely missing pieces are the campaign/staged-rollout server side, rollback semantics as requirements, and the module-firmware-over-CAN distribution path (that last one is well-spotted and correctly engages the §3.1 firmware-transfer FD-trigger clause via the spec-revision door). **(a) Segments / integration surfaces no lens covered**

- Telemetry-as-sensitive-data / privacy-DLP surface: nobody examined that kHz-class power traces are a workload side-channel (crypto/trading activity inference) and that the NanoKVM out-of-band vantage literally captures framebuffer/screen content — in the tier table's own financial/defense segments this makes CEC itself a data-exfiltration and data-governance object (classification, retention, GDPR/DLP review, per-customer data-flow disclosure). No lens produced requirements for it.
- Host-machine warranty and install-liability surface: inserting an interposer adds mated pairs and reseat cycles to melt-prone 12VHPWR/EPS paths — does CEC void the GPU/PSU/system OEM warranty, who carries liability for a connector event on a monitored machine, and what is the per-machine install labor/qualification story at 1k units? Untouched by all eight lenses (oem-integrator got closest but stopped at reliability skepticism).
- FPGA program surface: the owner-directed PolarFire path drags in Libero toolchain licensing, bitstream signing/update-at-fleet-scale (distinct from firmware OTA), FPGA development schedule/staffing risk, and single-vendor silicon dependence — procurement priced the part but no lens covered the data-plane *development and update* lifecycle.
- Upstream dependency sequencing: both tiers inherit the Hub Pro base (ESP32-P4, 8 ports, RS-485 receivers, OQ-5 topology unresolved) and Hub Pro is not built; no lens assessed that the Enterprise/MC program stacks behind an unbuilt tier-2 board and an open RS-485 topology decision.
- DCIM/NMS vendor-side partnership work: dcim-ops specified what protocols to speak but not the integration *program* — device-library/certification submissions (Sunbird/Nlyte/Device42), Redfish interop testing, Prometheus exporter maintenance — a staffing/GTM deliverable, not a firmware feature. Similarly uncovered: insurance/underwriter and hyperscaler/OCP-busbar segments as explicit in/out-of-scope calls.
- Host OS support matrix for the agent path (Linux headless servers, driver signing beyond Windows WHQL, container/VM deployments) — every lens critiqued USB-vs-network but none defined what hosts the in-band path must support.

**(b) Claims needing primary-source verification**

- EU CRA dates and scope (reporting 2026-09-11, full essential requirements 2027-12-11, applicability to a telemetry Hub and to non-networked Standard tier) — repeated verbatim by four lenses from one another; verify against the OJ regulation text before it anchors blocker status.
- Market-architecture claim that defense/broadcast/render/trading fleets are "predominantly dual-CRPS with no ATX harness" — an empirical claim that directly drives the module-family roadmap and contradicts other lenses' served-market framing; needs primary evidence (fleet composition data), not assertion.
- Specific priced/named facts: MPFS025T ~$69@1 DigiKey; Espressif 12-year longevity commitment; ~$300/node T1 media converters and 1000BASE-T1 15 m reach (T1 type A is 15 m but 40 m variants exist); FIPS 140-3 CMVP queue 12–18 months; ESP32-P4 native 10/100 EMAC; PolarFire Athena CAVP certificates and DPA-boot claims; Espressif absent from NDAA §889 covered list.
- Competitive-product claims: ASUS ROG Astral per-pin sensing via "IT8915FN" and the "Corsair PinProtect+" product name/capability; PDU ±1% accuracy being certified to IEC 62053-21 (a meter standard PDU vendors may only reference informally); NVIDIA PCAT specs. These will be quoted to customers — verify against vendor primary sources.
- MiFID II RTS 25 100 µs applicability — RTS 25 binds *trading event* timestamps, not facility monitoring gear; whether a power-telemetry device inherits that requirement (vs merely benefiting from PTP) is an inference the mc-verticals lens made without support.

**(c) Cross-lens contradictions the synthesis must reconcile**

- PolarFire vs "a $2 SE on the P4 is enough": security-compliance and oob-mgmt both argue Enterprise needs only P4+SE (100BASE-TX suffices; PolarFire is an MC/federal play), while competitive-landscape calls PolarFire fabric capture the moat — and the owner has already directed *both* enterprise variants onto PolarFire (D-ENT-2 resolved, plan §1a.1). The synthesis must present these as an explicit challenge-to-owner-direction with the cost consequence, not silently average them.
- Served-market contradiction: dcim-ops/oob-mgmt anchor the honest market on BMC-less ATX workstation/render/broadcast fleets; mission-critical-verticals says those same named verticals are mostly CRPS servers CEC physically cannot attach to. Both cannot be true as scoped; the requirements need a named target-fleet statement either way.

Three different end states for the same connector; the synthesis must pick one recommendation and note that Phase-2 research item 3 as scoped presumes the channel survives.
